data-model/jnode-navigation.md.text:
JNode navigation

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **JNode navigation** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-123 JNode cluster; JNodeTests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: JNode types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-jnode-types), [fn:jtree](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jtree), [fn:jkey](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jkey), [fn:jvalue](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jvalue), [XDM 4.0](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-datamodel-40/Overview.html). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #116](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/116), [immutable mainline revision `345ae58e`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/345ae58e5f8e35d1b504aa0a7df250e3eaf88dd0) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Navigate JSON keys with path syntax, then unwrap the selected JNode for its value. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use chained map lookup over parse-json output. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/jnode-navigation/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/jnode-navigation/main.xpath). Both yield `Utrecht` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A JSON order API sends a nested shipping address. Navigate JSON keys with path syntax, then unwrap the selected JNode for its value. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A missing key selects nothing. JNodes retain navigation context; plain map and array values have different identity semantics. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A missing key selects nothing. JNodes retain navigation context; plain map and array values have different identity semantics. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:jvalue(fn:jtree(map { 'shipping': map { 'city': 'Utrecht' } })/"shipping"/"city") ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences **Array member wrappers:** `array:members` returns one JNode per member, retaining empty and multi-item values with one-based keys. `array:of-members` reconstructs those wrapped values as separate members; a tested roundtrip preserves empty members, nested arrays and maps. These are released 4.0-only names, distinct from `array:items`. The [C05 matrix](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.json) records normal/empty/invalid/parent/type and lower-profile controls. Full generic-node identity/model/template support remains unsupported as described in the [model boundary](jnode-template-boundary.md). Benefit: Navigate JSON keys with path syntax, then unwrap the selected JNode for its value. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A missing key selects nothing. JNodes retain navigation context; plain map and array values have different identity semantics. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-jnode. Navigation, key/root/value type checks and array:members/array:of-members preserve member boundaries and empty/nested values. Generic node(), xnode() and is contracts remain unsupported model scope. Explicit jnode-pattern matching refuses XTSE0340 in both named hosts. The six generic-model unmet controls are retained known boundaries, not a new full-model adoption or template-rule certification. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/jnode-navigation/main.xpath) yields `Utrecht`. The [edge case](../examples/jnode-navigation/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: JNode construction plus path traversal. Building a navigation tree has a different allocation profile from direct map lookup. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `jnode-navigation-main`, `jnode-navigation-edge`, `jnode-navigation-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_JNodeFunctions_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0017`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_JNodeFunctions_FrozenXPath40_Work`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-jkey`, `fn-jtree`, `fn-jvalue`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.* **Scope review — 2026-10-12:** The [partial-model disposition](jnode-template-boundary.md) reconciles the original full-model exclusion with this shipped navigation. Eighteen additional checks supply full invoice input/output and explicit node()/xnode()/identity boundaries; navigation does not certify the complete generic model or stylesheet built-ins.

data-model/jnode-template-boundary.md.text:
JNode model and template boundary

Deferred remainder; partial Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **JNode model and template boundary — Deferred remainder; partial Frozen 4.0.** Shipped delivery remains [PR #116](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/116), [revision 345ae58e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/345ae58e5f8e35d1b504aa0a7df250e3eaf88dd0). Scope review: 2026-10-12, engine 1.1.2, [revision 3c0bd599](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee). This reconciles the [original full-model exclusion](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) with partial delivered support. Primary references: [XDM generic nodes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-datamodel-40/Overview.html#generic-nodes), [XPath JNode types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-jnode-types), [jtree](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jtree), [jkey](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jkey), [jvalue](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-jvalue), [XSLT built-in rules](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#built-in-rule). Immutable review sources: [XDM XML at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-datamodel-40/src/xpath-datamodel.xml), section `generic-nodes`, [function catalog](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml), and [XSLT source](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml). The review pin does not recover the missing historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Use shipped JSON navigation while keeping the broader generic-node type, identity and stylesheet contracts explicit. ## 3. Also Known As GNode means a generic node, collectively an XML node (XNode) or JSON wrapper node (JNode) in the reviewed draft. A plain map/array, a Bosak JNode wrapper and an IXdmNode XML adapter remain distinct values. ## 4. History / Supersedes REQ-118 originally excluded the full parallel model. REQ-123 subsequently delivered XdmJNode, jtree/jkey/jvalue, jnode type tests and navigation. That supersedes blanket wording that all JNode support is out of scope. The full unified model and JNode-specific stylesheet contracts remain uncertified. This review updates the original dossier rather than promoting the remainder. ## 5. Motivation A partner sends invoices as JSON. The application navigates array entries and nested keys to produce currency-labelled export rows. Parent context can help navigation, but consumers must not assume that XML-oriented node tests and identity operators already apply to every wrapper. ## 6. Language Alignment | Contract | Verified scope | |---|---| | Explicit jtree + child navigation + jvalue | Main, empty and reordered invoice reports work in Frozen 4.0 | | Plain map/array lookup | Portable 3.1 report produces the same rows for these inputs | | jkey on array children | 1-based positions `1|2` | | Parent navigation | Returns the enclosing invoice map; root parent empty | | jnode() test | Tested wrapper matches | | node() test on JNode | `false`; does not realize the draft's generic-node test | | xnode() on parsed XML | `XPST0051` in 3.1, 4.0 and experimental probes | | JNode identity with `is` | `XPTY0004`, even when both operands are the same wrapper | | Attribute axis on JNode | Empty in the tested case | | jvalue on a plain map | `XPTY0004`; unwrap only wrappers | Successful 4.0 cases retain the harness's default-3.1 refusal check. Error probes assert the declared marker, not a stage-specific diagnosis. This is scoped evidence, not exhaustive model conformance. ## 7. Applicability Choose 4.0 navigation when the host opts in and the wrapper operations meet the task. Retain portable map/array lookup for 3.1 integration. For stylesheet processing, unwrap JSON values and pass ordinary maps/arrays or construct XML explicitly; certify any additional template/model operation separately. ## 8. Structure The pinned model introduces a collective generic-node concept with node identity and order; `node()` covers GNodes and `xnode()` distinguishes XML nodes. Bosak stores JNode values separately from IXdmNode XML values. A wrapper records its value, entry key and parent; the root has no key/parent. Navigation support alone does not establish the common type and identity operators. ```xpath let $tree := jtree(map{'invoice':map{'id':'INV-1042'}}) return jvalue($tree/invoice/id/parent::*)?id ``` This is a complete parent-value operation; it is not an identity comparison or stylesheet rule dispatch. ## 9. Participants The host selects XPathCompatibility.XPath40. XdmJNode stores wrapper value/key/parent; the runtime navigates wrappers and the standard library creates/unwraps them. The invoice report formats scalar results. XML stylesheet source adapters remain a separate public integration surface. ## 10. Collaborations The 4.0 expression parses the full JSON, wraps the batch, navigates invoices and array members, then unwraps each invoice map. The portable expression traverses the same input by lookup. Both preserve invoice array order and keep currency with each total. They do not test universal equivalence of wrapper and map semantics. ## 11. Consequences The shipped feature is useful and should no longer be described as wholly absent. Confirmed broader gaps are node()/xnode() type alignment and JNode `is` identity. Default XSLT JNode rules, full generic-node ordering/union behavior and mixed-model operations are not certified here. No wrapper identity or stable map-key order is inferred from equal report strings. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-jnode. Navigation, key/root/value type checks and array:members/array:of-members preserve member boundaries and empty/nested values. Generic node(), xnode() and is contracts remain unsupported model scope. Explicit jnode-pattern matching refuses XTSE0340 in both named hosts. The six generic-model unmet controls are retained known boundaries, not a new full-model adoption or template-rule certification. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. Reviewed source: [XdmJNode.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Core/Xdm/XdmJNode.cs) stores Value/Key/Parent, while [VmEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) has JNode navigation/type branches but `EvaluateNodeComparison` requires IsNode operands. This explains the tested identity refusal. [TransformEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) and XML-oriented source APIs require separate review before claiming all draft JNode built-in template rules. Named existing evidence in [JNodeTests.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs): `Nav_ParentRoundTrip_ReturnsMapJNode`, `Nav_ChildOfArray_PositionKeyedJNodes`, `InstanceOf_Bare_MatchesAnyJNode`, `Nav_AttributeAxisOnJNode_IsEmpty`. Existing gate membership in [ConformanceRunner40.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) is `fn-jtree`, `fn-jkey`, `fn-jvalue`; membership is not a full generic-model gate. No gate is added or rerun in this documentation-only slice. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) adds eighteen checks, retaining the earlier `jnode-template-boundary-navigation` fixture. No engine/API/package changes. ## 13. Sample Code Complete invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or exchange conversion): ```json {"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]} ``` Complete Frozen 4.0 navigation report: ```xpath (: Partner invoice batch: navigate JNodes, unwrap each invoice map for reporting. :) let $tree := jtree(parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}')) return string-join($tree / invoices / * ! (let $invoice := jvalue(.) return concat($invoice?id, '/', $invoice?currency, ':', format-number($invoice?total, '0.00'))), ';') ``` Complete portable 3.1 alternative: ```xpath (: Portable 3.1: plain map/array lookup, without JNode identity or parent context. :) let $batch := parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}') return string-join($batch?invoices?* ! concat(?id, '/', ?currency, ':', format-number(?total, '0.00')), ';') ``` Both return exactly: ```text INV-1042/EUR:30.00;INV-1043/USD:12.00 ``` Empty input: ```json {"invoices":[]} ``` Both complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-empty.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-empty.xpath) expressions return the empty string. Reordered input: ```json {"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12},{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30}]} ``` The complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-reordered.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-reordered.xpath) expressions return: ```text INV-1043/USD:12.00;INV-1042/EUR:30.00 ``` Confirmed broader identity boundary: ```xpath let $tree := jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) return $tree is $tree ``` Result: `XPTY0004`. Complete node-type probes: ```xpath jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) instance of node() ``` Result: `false`. ```xpath parse-xml('') instance of xnode() ``` Result: `XPST0051`. All new fixtures are linked below; output uses JSON string notation for empty values. The review pin does not recover the missing historical adopted specification snapshot.
sections.2: Use shipped JSON navigation while keeping the broader generic-node type, identity and stylesheet contracts explicit.
sections.3: GNode means a generic node, collectively an XML node (XNode) or JSON wrapper node (JNode) in the reviewed draft. A plain map/array, a Bosak JNode wrapper and an IXdmNode XML adapter remain distinct values.
sections.4: REQ-118 originally excluded the full parallel model. REQ-123 subsequently delivered XdmJNode, jtree/jkey/jvalue, jnode type tests and navigation. That supersedes blanket wording that all JNode support is out of scope. The full unified model and JNode-specific stylesheet contracts remain uncertified. This review updates the original dossier rather than promoting the remainder.
sections.5: A partner sends invoices as JSON. The application navigates array entries and nested keys to produce currency-labelled export rows. Parent context can help navigation, but consumers must not assume that XML-oriented node tests and identity operators already apply to every wrapper.
sections.6:
| Contract | Verified scope |
|---|---|
| Explicit jtree + child navigation + jvalue | Main, empty and reordered invoice reports work in Frozen 4.0 |
| Plain map/array lookup | Portable 3.1 report produces the same rows for these inputs |
| jkey on array children | 1-based positions `1|2` |
| Parent navigation | Returns the enclosing invoice map; root parent empty |
| jnode() test | Tested wrapper matches |
| node() test on JNode | `false`; does not realize the draft's generic-node test |
| xnode() on parsed XML | `XPST0051` in 3.1, 4.0 and experimental probes |
| JNode identity with `is` | `XPTY0004`, even when both operands are the same wrapper |
| Attribute axis on JNode | Empty in the tested case |
| jvalue on a plain map | `XPTY0004`; unwrap only wrappers |

Successful 4.0 cases retain the harness's default-3.1 refusal check. Error probes assert the declared marker, not a stage-specific diagnosis. This is scoped evidence, not exhaustive model conformance.
sections.7: Choose 4.0 navigation when the host opts in and the wrapper operations meet the task. Retain portable map/array lookup for 3.1 integration. For stylesheet processing, unwrap JSON values and pass ordinary maps/arrays or construct XML explicitly; certify any additional template/model operation separately.
sections.8:
The pinned model introduces a collective generic-node concept with node identity and order; `node()` covers GNodes and `xnode()` distinguishes XML nodes. Bosak stores JNode values separately from IXdmNode XML values. A wrapper records its value, entry key and parent; the root has no key/parent. Navigation support alone does not establish the common type and identity operators.

```xpath
let $tree := jtree(map{'invoice':map{'id':'INV-1042'}})
return jvalue($tree/invoice/id/parent::*)?id
```

This is a complete parent-value operation; it is not an identity comparison or stylesheet rule dispatch.
sections.9: The host selects XPathCompatibility.XPath40. XdmJNode stores wrapper value/key/parent; the runtime navigates wrappers and the standard library creates/unwraps them. The invoice report formats scalar results. XML stylesheet source adapters remain a separate public integration surface.
sections.10: The 4.0 expression parses the full JSON, wraps the batch, navigates invoices and array members, then unwraps each invoice map. The portable expression traverses the same input by lookup. Both preserve invoice array order and keep currency with each total. They do not test universal equivalence of wrapper and map semantics.
sections.11: The shipped feature is useful and should no longer be described as wholly absent. Confirmed broader gaps are node()/xnode() type alignment and JNode `is` identity. Default XSLT JNode rules, full generic-node ordering/union behavior and mixed-model operations are not certified here. No wrapper identity or stable map-key order is inferred from equal report strings.
sections.12:
**C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-jnode. Navigation, key/root/value type checks and array:members/array:of-members preserve member boundaries and empty/nested values. Generic node(), xnode() and is contracts remain unsupported model scope. Explicit jnode-pattern matching refuses XTSE0340 in both named hosts. The six generic-model unmet controls are retained known boundaries, not a new full-model adoption or template-rule certification. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows.


Reviewed source: [XdmJNode.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Core/Xdm/XdmJNode.cs) stores Value/Key/Parent, while [VmEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) has JNode navigation/type branches but `EvaluateNodeComparison` requires IsNode operands. This explains the tested identity refusal. [TransformEngine.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) and XML-oriented source APIs require separate review before claiming all draft JNode built-in template rules.

Named existing evidence in [JNodeTests.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/JNodeTests.cs): `Nav_ParentRoundTrip_ReturnsMapJNode`, `Nav_ChildOfArray_PositionKeyedJNodes`, `InstanceOf_Bare_MatchesAnyJNode`, `Nav_AttributeAxisOnJNode_IsEmpty`. Existing gate membership in [ConformanceRunner40.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/3c0bd5994baf4fa85b1db5805fc5c081d63c50ee/tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) is `fn-jtree`, `fn-jkey`, `fn-jvalue`; membership is not a full generic-model gate. No gate is added or rerun in this documentation-only slice.

The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) adds eighteen checks, retaining the earlier `jnode-template-boundary-navigation` fixture. No engine/API/package changes.
sections.13:
Complete invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or exchange conversion):

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}
```

Complete Frozen 4.0 navigation report:

```xpath
(: Partner invoice batch: navigate JNodes, unwrap each invoice map for reporting. :)
let $tree := jtree(parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}'))
return string-join($tree / invoices / * ! (let $invoice := jvalue(.) return concat($invoice?id, '/', $invoice?currency, ':', format-number($invoice?total, '0.00'))), ';')
```

Complete portable 3.1 alternative:

```xpath
(: Portable 3.1: plain map/array lookup, without JNode identity or parent context. :)
let $batch := parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12}]}')
return string-join($batch?invoices?* ! concat(?id, '/', ?currency, ':', format-number(?total, '0.00')), ';')
```

Both return exactly:

```text
INV-1042/EUR:30.00;INV-1043/USD:12.00
```

Empty input:

```json
{"invoices":[]}
```

Both complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-empty.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-empty.xpath) expressions return the empty string. Reordered input:

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12},{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30}]}
```

The complete [navigation](../examples/jnode-scope/navigation-reordered.xpath) and [portable](../examples/jnode-scope/portable-reordered.xpath) expressions return:

```text
INV-1043/USD:12.00;INV-1042/EUR:30.00
```

Confirmed broader identity boundary:

```xpath
let $tree := jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) return $tree is $tree
```

Result: `XPTY0004`. Complete node-type probes:

```xpath
jtree(map{'id':'INV-1042'}) instance of node()
```

Result: `false`.

```xpath
parse-xml('<invoice/>') instance of xnode()
```

Result: `XPST0051`.

deferred/capturing-accumulators.md.text:
Capturing accumulators

Deferred — attribute acceptance does not create a snapshot

## 1. Name and Classification **Capturing accumulators — Deferred.** [REQ-118 tier-4 decision](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) records the deferral. Bosak reviewed 2026-10-12 at [revision 7c827ace](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/7c827ace77b917c130bba81f8599984ce54ab809), engine 1.1.2. This is a disposition reference, not implementation of capture semantics. External reference: [XSLT 4.0 capturing accumulators](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#capturing-accumulators). Immutable review source: [QT4CG xslt.xml at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), ID `capturing-accumulators`, issue 211 / PR 717 (2023-09-29). This review does not recover the historical adopted specification pin. ## 2. Intent Retain an invoice subtree after visiting it, so a later report can inspect its line children without depending on the original streamed node. ## 3. Also Known As End-phase accumulator capture. It is distinct from ordinary accumulator values, explicit `snapshot()`, result capture through `CaptureTransform`, and authoring snapshots. ## 4. History / Supersedes The reviewed draft evaluates an end-phase capturing rule against a snapshot copy of a matched element, excluding accumulator values from that copy. It applies in both streamed and ordinary evaluation; non-element matches are unaffected. Bosak's deferral is not superseded by accepting the attribute or by implementing ordinary accumulators/snapshots. ## 5. Motivation A batch exporter might retain the latest invoice for deferred line inspection. On an in-memory tree, retaining the original node can look correct because its children remain available. Node identity distinguishes that behavior from an actual copied subtree, preventing an in-memory pass from being mistaken for capture support. ## 6. Language Alignment | Tested form | Observed Bosak outcome | |---|---| | `phase="end" capture="yes"`, stylesheet 4.0 or 3.0 | Accumulator value is the original invoice (`is` returns true) | | Capture absent or `no` | Same source-node identity | | Invalid capture value, or start-phase capture, at version 4.0 | Tolerated; same source-node identity | | Ordinary 3.0 accumulator without capture | Retains the source node as declared by `select="."` | | Explicit `snapshot(.)` in the template | New node identity (`is` returns false), line children preserved | | Scalar ordinary counter | Three visited line elements in the fixture | The draft capture rule must use end phase, and capture would change the identity of an element-context copy. The observed ignored-attribute cases are limitations against that contract, not draft conformance. No stream execution is tested by these catalog fixtures. ## 7. Applicability Use an ordinary accumulator for scalar counts or source-node references on an in-memory tree. Use an explicit snapshot when an independent copied node is needed in this verified in-memory workflow. If only ID/line counts are needed, project those values instead of retaining a subtree. None of these alternatives proves streamable capture or the draft's special exclusion of accumulator annotations. ## 8. Structure An ordinary accumulator stores the latest invoice at end phase. The invoice template retrieves its after-value and reports ID, identity and line count. A separate snapshot alternative copies the invoice in the template. A projection alternative reports ID/count directly without retaining XML. ## 9. Participants [AccumulatorDefinition](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/AccumulatorDefinition.cs) parses rule match/select/phase; it does not model the capture option. [TransformEngine](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) walks source nodes and applies ordinary rules using their source-node focus. [FunctionLibrary](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs) supplies ordinary snapshot behavior. [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles exact files and runs in-memory capture. ## 10. Collaborations `use-accumulators`, `accumulator-after`, `snapshot`, node identity `is`, `count` and ordered template application support the example. `CaptureTransform` captures principal result bytes; its name does not indicate capturing-accumulator implementation. ## 11. Consequences The capture attribute cannot be used as a support detector. Tests with accessible source descendants alone would miss the gap; the identity assertions expose it. Explicit snapshots allocate copies and may carry ordinary accumulator semantics; this example does not verify the capture rule's no-accumulator-values exception. Keeping many snapshots can retain substantial memory. The report projects fixture values and does not validate invoice data. ## 12. Implementation `AccumulatorRule.FromElement` reads match/select/phase without capture; `ComputeAccumulatorValues` visits source nodes and `ApplyAccumulatorRule` evaluates against that focus. The successful invalid/start-phase probes do not establish draft option/phase validation. Registered-but-unknown accumulator access raises XTDE3341 in the targeted fixture; an accumulator excluded by the mode raises XTDE3362. These are ordinary accumulator boundaries. No engine changes or gate promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code Complete [batch input](../examples/capturing-accumulators/input.xml): ```xml ``` Complete [capture identity probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/main-observed.xsl): ```xml ``` Observed principal text output: ```text INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1; ``` This is original-node retention, not the draft-required copy. The [version 3.0 probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture31.xsl) has the same observed result; the [ordinary 3.0 form](../examples/capturing-accumulators/ordinary31.xsl) removes the capture attribute and honestly expresses source retention. ### Explicit snapshot alternative Complete [XSLT 3.0 snapshot stylesheet](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot31.xsl): ```xml ``` Output: ```text INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;INV-2049:source=false:lines=1; ``` Line children survive the copy and identity differs. This snapshot is made in an ordinary template using an in-memory source; it does not enable the deferred rule or certify streaming memory behavior. ### Scalar projection alternative Complete [XSLT 3.0 projection](../examples/capturing-accumulators/projection31.xsl): ```xml ``` Output: ```text INV-2048:lines=2;INV-2049:lines=1; ``` ### Empty and reordered input Complete empty input: ```xml ``` The capture, snapshot and projection empty fixtures return the empty string. Complete reordered input: ```xml ``` Snapshot output: ```text INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;INV-2048:source=false:lines=2; ``` ### Complete fixture inventory The [manifest](../examples/cases.json) executes 16 cases through the in-memory catalog harness. Errors verify compile/capture markers, without promising a universal detection stage. | Fixture | Mode | Exact output/error marker | |---|---|---| | [main-observed](../examples/capturing-accumulators/main-observed.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [capture-no](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture-no.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [capture-absent](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture-absent.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [invalid-capture-observed](../examples/capturing-accumulators/invalid-capture-observed.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [start-capture-observed](../examples/capturing-accumulators/start-capture-observed.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [capture31](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture31.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [capture-empty](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture-empty.xsl) | xslt40 | `` | | [ordinary31](../examples/capturing-accumulators/ordinary31.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;` | | [snapshot31](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot31.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;` | | [snapshot-empty](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot-empty.xsl) | xslt31 | `` | | [snapshot-reordered](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot-reordered.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;` | | [projection31](../examples/capturing-accumulators/projection31.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:lines=2;INV-2049:lines=1;` | | [projection-empty](../examples/capturing-accumulators/projection-empty.xsl) | xslt31 | `` | | [ordinary-counter](../examples/capturing-accumulators/ordinary-counter.xsl) | xslt31 | `3` | | [unknown-accumulator](../examples/capturing-accumulators/unknown-accumulator.xsl) | xslt31 | `XTDE3341` | | [not-applicable](../examples/capturing-accumulators/not-applicable.xsl) | xslt31 | `XTDE3362` | ## 14. Performance An ordinary node-valued accumulator retains source nodes. Snapshot copies require memory for copied content; retaining snapshots affects lifetime. A scalar projection avoids retained subtree copies. No capturing-accumulator benchmark, bounded-memory guarantee or streaming certification is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses This invoice case is synthetic integration evidence. Existing [StreamingAccumulatorTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/StreamingAccumulatorTests.cs) include `CounterAccumulator_Parity`, `SumWithAccumulatorAfter_Parity`, `UnknownAccumulator_ThrowsXTDE3341` and `InapplicableAccumulator_ThrowsXTDE3362` for ordinary accumulator paths. [StreamingSnapshotTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/StreamingSnapshotTests.cs) includes `SnapshotDocumentNode_ParityWithInMemory` and `SnapshotShellRoot_KeepsDocumentParent`. These named streaming tests are separate evidence, not capture-rule conformance or catalog streaming tests. No gate membership changes are included. ## 16. Related Features [Enclosing modes](enclosing-modes.md), [computed XPath constructors](computed-node-constructors.md), [completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) and [supplementary audit](../SUPPLEMENTARY-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md).

This is a disposition reference, not implementation of capture semantics.
External reference: [XSLT 4.0 capturing accumulators](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#capturing-accumulators). Immutable review source: [QT4CG xslt.xml at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), ID `capturing-accumulators`, issue 211 / PR 717 (2023-09-29). This review does not recover the historical adopted specification pin.
sections.2: Retain an invoice subtree after visiting it, so a later report can inspect its line children without depending on the original streamed node.
sections.3: End-phase accumulator capture. It is distinct from ordinary accumulator values, explicit `snapshot()`, result capture through `CaptureTransform`, and authoring snapshots.
sections.4: The reviewed draft evaluates an end-phase capturing rule against a snapshot copy of a matched element, excluding accumulator values from that copy. It applies in both streamed and ordinary evaluation; non-element matches are unaffected. Bosak's deferral is not superseded by accepting the attribute or by implementing ordinary accumulators/snapshots.
sections.5: A batch exporter might retain the latest invoice for deferred line inspection. On an in-memory tree, retaining the original node can look correct because its children remain available. Node identity distinguishes that behavior from an actual copied subtree, preventing an in-memory pass from being mistaken for capture support.
sections.6:
| Tested form | Observed Bosak outcome |
|---|---|
| `phase="end" capture="yes"`, stylesheet 4.0 or 3.0 | Accumulator value is the original invoice (`is` returns true) |
| Capture absent or `no` | Same source-node identity |
| Invalid capture value, or start-phase capture, at version 4.0 | Tolerated; same source-node identity |
| Ordinary 3.0 accumulator without capture | Retains the source node as declared by `select="."` |
| Explicit `snapshot(.)` in the template | New node identity (`is` returns false), line children preserved |
| Scalar ordinary counter | Three visited line elements in the fixture |

The draft capture rule must use end phase, and capture would change the identity of an element-context copy. The observed ignored-attribute cases are limitations against that contract, not draft conformance. No stream execution is tested by these catalog fixtures.
sections.7: Use an ordinary accumulator for scalar counts or source-node references on an in-memory tree. Use an explicit snapshot when an independent copied node is needed in this verified in-memory workflow. If only ID/line counts are needed, project those values instead of retaining a subtree. None of these alternatives proves streamable capture or the draft's special exclusion of accumulator annotations.
sections.8: An ordinary accumulator stores the latest invoice at end phase. The invoice template retrieves its after-value and reports ID, identity and line count. A separate snapshot alternative copies the invoice in the template. A projection alternative reports ID/count directly without retaining XML.
sections.9: [AccumulatorDefinition](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/AccumulatorDefinition.cs) parses rule match/select/phase; it does not model the capture option. [TransformEngine](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) walks source nodes and applies ordinary rules using their source-node focus. [FunctionLibrary](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs) supplies ordinary snapshot behavior. [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles exact files and runs in-memory capture.
sections.10: `use-accumulators`, `accumulator-after`, `snapshot`, node identity `is`, `count` and ordered template application support the example. `CaptureTransform` captures principal result bytes; its name does not indicate capturing-accumulator implementation.
sections.11: The capture attribute cannot be used as a support detector. Tests with accessible source descendants alone would miss the gap; the identity assertions expose it. Explicit snapshots allocate copies and may carry ordinary accumulator semantics; this example does not verify the capture rule's no-accumulator-values exception. Keeping many snapshots can retain substantial memory. The report projects fixture values and does not validate invoice data.
sections.12: `AccumulatorRule.FromElement` reads match/select/phase without capture; `ComputeAccumulatorValues` visits source nodes and `ApplyAccumulatorRule` evaluates against that focus. The successful invalid/start-phase probes do not establish draft option/phase validation. Registered-but-unknown accumulator access raises XTDE3341 in the targeted fixture; an accumulator excluded by the mode raises XTDE3362. These are ordinary accumulator boundaries. No engine changes or gate promotions are included.
sections.13:
Complete [batch input](../examples/capturing-accumulators/input.xml):

```xml
<batch><invoice id="INV-2048" currency="EUR"><line sku="P100"/><line sku="P200"/></invoice><invoice id="INV-2049" currency="USD"><line sku="P300"/></invoice></batch>
```

Complete [capture identity probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/main-observed.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred capturing accumulators and in-memory invoice alternatives.
SPECIAL NOTES: Capture attribute acceptance is not snapshot support; no streaming claim.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="4.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:accumulator name="latest" initial-value="()">
    <xsl:accumulator-rule match="invoice" phase="end" capture="yes" select="."/>
  </xsl:accumulator>
  <xsl:mode use-accumulators="latest"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:variable name="last" select="accumulator-after('latest')"/>
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':source=', $last is ., ':lines=', count($last/line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Observed principal text output:

```text
INV-2048:source=true:lines=2;INV-2049:source=true:lines=1;
```

This is original-node retention, not the draft-required copy. The [version 3.0 probe](../examples/capturing-accumulators/capture31.xsl) has the same observed result; the [ordinary 3.0 form](../examples/capturing-accumulators/ordinary31.xsl) removes the capture attribute and honestly expresses source retention.

### Explicit snapshot alternative

Complete [XSLT 3.0 snapshot stylesheet](../examples/capturing-accumulators/snapshot31.xsl):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Verify deferred capturing accumulators and in-memory invoice alternatives.
SPECIAL NOTES: Capture attribute acceptance is not snapshot support; no streaming claim.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation
Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:variable name="copy" select="snapshot(.)"/>
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':source=', $copy is ., ':lines=', count($copy/line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;
```

Line children survive the copy and identity differs. This snapshot is made in an ordinary template using an in-memory source; it does not enable the deferred rule or certify streaming memory behavior.

### Scalar projection alternative

Complete [XSLT 3.0 projection](../examples/capturing-accumulators/projection31.xsl):

```xml

Input: batch/invoice id and line children. Output: exact identity/line-count report.
The retained ordinary accumulator value is a source node. Explicit snapshot creates
a new node; it is not the capture rule's special no-accumulator-values contract.
All catalog cases use ordinary in-memory CaptureTransform, not TransformStreaming.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" version="3.0">
  <xsl:output method="text"/>
  <xsl:template match="/">
    <xsl:apply-templates select="batch/invoice"/>
  </xsl:template>
  <xsl:template match="invoice">
    <xsl:value-of select="concat(@id, ':lines=', count(line), ';')"/>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Output:

```text
INV-2048:lines=2;INV-2049:lines=1;
```

### Empty and reordered input

Complete empty input:

```xml
<batch/>
```

The capture, snapshot and projection empty fixtures return the empty string. Complete reordered input:

```xml

```

Snapshot output:

```text
INV-2049:source=false:lines=1;INV-2048:source=false:lines=2;
```

deferred/computed-node-constructors.md.text:
Computed XPath node constructors

Deferred in Bosak XPath — use the appropriate XML construction host

## 1. Name and Classification **Computed XPath node constructors — Deferred.** [REQ-118 tier-2 decision](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) records the original deferral: February-2026 draft movement and overlap with existing XQuery construction. Bosak source reviewed 2026-10-12 at [revision 28d8dccc](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/28d8dccc74ab35e27db92584a7bc3e1a202b7cb5) (URI documentation delivery; engine version 1.1.2). This is a new disposition record, not a constructor implementation or tier promotion. External reference: [XPath 4.0 node constructors](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-constructors). Immutable review source: [QT4CG expressions.xml at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), IDs `id-constructors` and `id-computedConstructors`. The source records addition to XPath on 2026-02-07 (issue 2427 / PR 2446), and name-coercion changes on 2026-05-23. This current review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. The draft includes the feature; Bosak retains its deferral. ## 2. Intent Create an ERP receipt from a supplier invoice, computing element/attribute content from the source. Keep XPath evaluation separate from the host that constructs XML nodes. ## 3. Also Known As Computed node construction; element, attribute, document, text, comment, processing-instruction and namespace constructors. These are syntax productions, distinct from `xs:*` atomic constructor functions and map/array constructors. ## 4. History / Supersedes XQuery 3.1 already has [computed constructors](https://www.w3.org/TR/xquery-31/#id-computedConstructors). The reviewed XPath 4.0 draft adds them to XPath. Bosak's shared parser already supports XQuery construction, but its `_allowFullFlwor` host flag controls recognition independently of XPath 4.0 compatibility. The historical deferral has not been superseded by enabling the 4.0 flag. ## 5. Motivation A receipt export needs real XML node construction, escaping and attribute ordering. A successful XQuery constructor test does not establish that the same source compiles through `XPath31Expression`. The complete XSLT alternative below constructs the receipt without manually escaping source strings. ## 6. Language Alignment | Host / mode | Verified boundary | |---|---| | XPath31, XPath40, XPath40Experimental | Seven computed node-kind forms and direct XML element syntax refuse with `XPST0003` | | XQuery 3.1 | Existing computed-constructor tests exercise all seven kinds and selected dynamic errors | | XSLT 3.0 | Node instructions/literal result elements construct the complete receipt | The pinned draft requires named XPath constructors to use a QName literal such as `element #receipt { ... }`, or a name expression such as `element { 'receipt' } { ... }`. Bare names in earlier XQuery syntax, such as `element receipt { ... }`, are not the reviewed XPath grammar. Refusal fixtures use braced names valid in that draft. Direct `` syntax remains a separate XQuery-only alternative, not a promised XPath 4.0 form. No full XQuery 4.0 grammar claim follows from the 3.1 tests. ## 7. Applicability Use the disposition when selecting an XML export architecture. Use XSLT for document transformation, or the XQuery API for existing XQuery construction contracts. XPath can select source values and construct maps/arrays; that does not create XML nodes. `parse-xml` parses existing XML text, and is not a substitute for arbitrary safe node construction by string concatenation. ## 8. Structure Invoice XML → select customer/amount → XSLT element/attribute/value instructions → receipt XML. The refused XPath expression shows the same intended projection, but produces no output in Bosak. ## 9. Participants `XPath31Expression` is the refusing host. The shared [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) recognizes constructors only under `_allowFullFlwor`. [XQueryParser](../../../src/Bosak.XQuery/Parser/XQueryParser.cs) supplies that host flag. [XQueryCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.XQuery/Api/XQueryCompiler.cs) is the supported query entry point; XSLT supplies the transformation alternative. ## 10. Collaborations `parse-xml`, `string` and `concat` support the 3.1 text report. XSLT `xsl:element`, `xsl:attribute`, literal result elements and `xsl:value-of` produce XML. Attribute instructions execute before child content. The serializer handles the ampersand in `Ada & Co`. ## 11. Consequences Opting into XPath40Experimental does not unlock this feature. A consumer must choose a construction host; do not retry the same XPath expression with a higher mode. The 3.1 report preserves business values but is a text report, not equivalent XML output. The example projects supplied strings without validating money/currency. Empty customer content yields an empty element; the exact tested serializer spelling is ``. ## 12. Implementation Parser evidence: `Parse` sets `allowConstructors: allowFullFlwor` in the lexer; `ParsePrimaryExpr` and the axis-step recognition guard `IsComputedConstructorForm` with `_allowFullFlwor`. `xpath40` alone does not satisfy it. XQueryParser calls the shared parser with `allowFullFlwor: true`. No parser/runtime changes or conformance promotions are part of this record. ## 13. Sample Code Complete [invoice input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/input.xml): ```xml Ada & Co125.50 ``` Complete [refused XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/main-refusal.xpath): ```xpath let $i := parse-xml('Ada & Co125.50')/invoice return element { 'receipt' } { attribute { 'id' } { string($i/@id) }, element { 'customer' } { string($i/customer) }, element { 'total' } { attribute { 'currency' } { string($i/amount/@currency) }, string($i/amount) } } ``` Observed outcome: `XPST0003`; no constructed receipt is returned. ### XPath 3.1 report alternative Complete [text-report fixture](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $i := parse-xml('Ada & Co125.50')/invoice return concat('id=', $i/@id, '; customer=', $i/customer, '; total=', $i/amount, ' ', $i/amount/@currency) ``` Output: ```text id=INV-2048; customer=Ada & Co; total=125.50 EUR ``` ### Complete XSLT 3.0 construction alternative The [stylesheet](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/xslt-main.xsl) consumes the input above, using `/invoice` as its template context. It documents its projection contract and empty-content boundary inside the file. ```xml ``` Principal output (no secondary output): ```xml Ada & Co125.50 ``` Complete [empty-customer input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/empty.xml): ```xml 0.00 ``` Output: ```xml 0.00 ``` ### Existing XQuery evidence The existing `XQuery_ComputedElement_ComputedNameAndAtomicContent` test evaluates: ```xquery (name(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 }), string(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 })) ``` It asserts two string items, `dyn` and `1 2 3`, through `XQueryCompiler` and `XQueryContext`. This is named unit-test evidence, not a new XQuery manifest fixture or proof that XPath constructors work. ### Complete fixture inventory The [manifest](../examples/cases.json) and [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) execute 30 new cases: 25 XPath refusals, three 3.1 reports and two XSLT outputs. Error markers assert the host boundary, not full draft constructor semantics. | Fixture | Mode | Exact output/error marker | |---|---|---| | [element-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/element-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [element-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/element-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [element-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/element-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [attribute-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/attribute-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [attribute-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/attribute-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [attribute-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/attribute-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [document-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/document-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [document-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/document-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [document-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/document-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [text-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/text-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [text-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/text-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [text-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/text-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [comment-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/comment-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [comment-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/comment-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [comment-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/comment-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [processing-instruction-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/processing-instruction-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [processing-instruction-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/processing-instruction-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [processing-instruction-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/processing-instruction-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [namespace-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/namespace-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [namespace-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/namespace-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [namespace-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/namespace-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [direct-element-31](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/direct-element-31.xpath) | 31 | `XPST0003` | | [direct-element-40](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/direct-element-40.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [direct-element-experimental](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/direct-element-experimental.xpath) | experimental | `XPST0003` | | [main-refusal](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/main-refusal.xpath) | 40 | `XPST0003` | | [baseline](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline.xpath) | 31 | `id=INV-2048; customer=Ada & Co; total=125.50 EUR` | | [baseline-empty](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline-empty.xpath) | 31 | `id=INV-EMPTY; customer=; total=0.00 EUR` | | [baseline-escaped](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline-escaped.xpath) | 31 | `id=INV-SPECIAL; customer=A < B & C; total=7.00 EUR` | | [xslt-main](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/xslt-main.xsl) | 31 | `Ada & Co125.50` | | [xslt-empty](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/xslt-empty.xsl) | 31 | `0.00` | ## 14. Performance Refusal happens during XPath compilation. XSLT constructs and serializes an output tree; costs depend on the input and transformation. No benchmark or performance comparison with deferred XPath constructors is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses The receipt projection is a synthetic ERP integration case. Existing [XQuery tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XQuery.Tests/PlaceholderTests.cs) include `XQuery_ComputedElement_StaticName`, `XQuery_ComputedElement_ComputedNameAndAtomicContent`, `XQuery_ComputedElement_EmptyContent`, `XQuery_ComputedAttribute_AddsToElement`, `XQuery_ComputedTextCommentAndPI`, `XQuery_ComputedDocument_WrapsContent`, `XQuery_ComputedNamespace_BecomesDeclaration`, `XQuery_ComputedComment_DoubleHyphen_Rejected`, `XQuery_ComputedPI_NestedTerminator_Rejected` and `XQuery_ComputedAttribute_AfterContent_Rejected`. The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no computed-node-constructor assignment in GatedSets. Its `misc-FocusConstructors` gate covers atomic focus constructor functions, a separate feature. Existing tests and refusal fixtures do not certify XPath 4.0 node construction. ## 16. Related Features [Invoice-to-ERP worked chapter](../worked-examples/invoice-to-erp/README.md), [XPath switch disposition](../rejected/xpath-switch-expression.md), [completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) and [supplementary audit](../SUPPLEMENTARY-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md).

The source records addition to XPath on 2026-02-07 (issue 2427 / PR 2446), and name-coercion changes on 2026-05-23. This current review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. The draft includes the feature; Bosak retains its deferral.
sections.2: Create an ERP receipt from a supplier invoice, computing element/attribute content from the source. Keep XPath evaluation separate from the host that constructs XML nodes.
sections.3: Computed node construction; element, attribute, document, text, comment, processing-instruction and namespace constructors. These are syntax productions, distinct from `xs:*` atomic constructor functions and map/array constructors.
sections.4: XQuery 3.1 already has [computed constructors](https://www.w3.org/TR/xquery-31/#id-computedConstructors). The reviewed XPath 4.0 draft adds them to XPath. Bosak's shared parser already supports XQuery construction, but its `_allowFullFlwor` host flag controls recognition independently of XPath 4.0 compatibility. The historical deferral has not been superseded by enabling the 4.0 flag.
sections.5: A receipt export needs real XML node construction, escaping and attribute ordering. A successful XQuery constructor test does not establish that the same source compiles through `XPath31Expression`. The complete XSLT alternative below constructs the receipt without manually escaping source strings.
sections.6:
| Host / mode | Verified boundary |
|---|---|
| XPath31, XPath40, XPath40Experimental | Seven computed node-kind forms and direct XML element syntax refuse with `XPST0003` |
| XQuery 3.1 | Existing computed-constructor tests exercise all seven kinds and selected dynamic errors |
| XSLT 3.0 | Node instructions/literal result elements construct the complete receipt |

The pinned draft requires named XPath constructors to use a QName literal such as `element #receipt { ... }`, or a name expression such as `element { 'receipt' } { ... }`. Bare names in earlier XQuery syntax, such as `element receipt { ... }`, are not the reviewed XPath grammar. Refusal fixtures use braced names valid in that draft. Direct `<receipt/>` syntax remains a separate XQuery-only alternative, not a promised XPath 4.0 form. No full XQuery 4.0 grammar claim follows from the 3.1 tests.
sections.7: Use the disposition when selecting an XML export architecture. Use XSLT for document transformation, or the XQuery API for existing XQuery construction contracts. XPath can select source values and construct maps/arrays; that does not create XML nodes. `parse-xml` parses existing XML text, and is not a substitute for arbitrary safe node construction by string concatenation.
sections.8: Invoice XML → select customer/amount → XSLT element/attribute/value instructions → receipt XML. The refused XPath expression shows the same intended projection, but produces no output in Bosak.
sections.9: `XPath31Expression` is the refusing host. The shared [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) recognizes constructors only under `_allowFullFlwor`. [XQueryParser](../../../src/Bosak.XQuery/Parser/XQueryParser.cs) supplies that host flag. [XQueryCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.XQuery/Api/XQueryCompiler.cs) is the supported query entry point; XSLT supplies the transformation alternative.
sections.10: `parse-xml`, `string` and `concat` support the 3.1 text report. XSLT `xsl:element`, `xsl:attribute`, literal result elements and `xsl:value-of` produce XML. Attribute instructions execute before child content. The serializer handles the ampersand in `Ada & Co`.
sections.11: Opting into XPath40Experimental does not unlock this feature. A consumer must choose a construction host; do not retry the same XPath expression with a higher mode. The 3.1 report preserves business values but is a text report, not equivalent XML output. The example projects supplied strings without validating money/currency. Empty customer content yields an empty element; the exact tested serializer spelling is `<customer/>`.
sections.12: Parser evidence: `Parse` sets `allowConstructors: allowFullFlwor` in the lexer; `ParsePrimaryExpr` and the axis-step recognition guard `IsComputedConstructorForm` with `_allowFullFlwor`. `xpath40` alone does not satisfy it. XQueryParser calls the shared parser with `allowFullFlwor: true`. No parser/runtime changes or conformance promotions are part of this record.
sections.13:
Complete [invoice input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/input.xml):

```xml
<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>
```

Complete [refused XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/main-refusal.xpath):

```xpath
let $i := parse-xml('<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>')/invoice
return element { 'receipt' } { attribute { 'id' } { string($i/@id) }, element { 'customer' } { string($i/customer) }, element { 'total' } { attribute { 'currency' } { string($i/amount/@currency) }, string($i/amount) } }
```

Observed outcome: `XPST0003`; no constructed receipt is returned.

### XPath 3.1 report alternative

Complete [text-report fixture](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $i := parse-xml('<invoice id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><amount currency="EUR">125.50</amount></invoice>')/invoice return concat('id=', $i/@id, '; customer=', $i/customer, '; total=', $i/amount, ' ', $i/amount/@currency)
```

Output:

```text
id=INV-2048; customer=Ada & Co; total=125.50 EUR
```

### Complete XSLT 3.0 construction alternative

The [stylesheet](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/xslt-main.xsl) consumes the input above, using `/invoice` as its template context. It documents its projection contract and empty-content boundary inside the file.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
AUTHOR: Charles Korthout
CREATE DATE: 12 October 2026
PURPOSE: Project a supplier invoice into an ERP receipt using portable XSLT 3.0.
SPECIAL NOTES: Alternative to deferred computed XPath node constructors; no external I/O.
COPYRIGHT: Fytala
LICENSE: license.md (Apache-2.0)
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
Change History: Charles Korthout | 0.1 | 12-10-2026 | Creation

Input contract: invoice/@id, customer text, amount text and amount/@currency.
The stylesheet projects supplied strings; it does not validate currency or totals.
XSLT node construction escapes XML characters through the serializer.
Empty customer content creates an empty customer element. Attribute instructions
precede child nodes. No computed XPath constructor expression is required.
-->
<xsl:stylesheet version="3.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">
  <xsl:output method="xml" omit-xml-declaration="yes" indent="no"/>
  <xsl:template match="/invoice">
    <xsl:element name="receipt">
      <xsl:attribute name="id" select="string(@id)"/>
      <customer><xsl:value-of select="customer"/></customer>
      <total><xsl:attribute name="currency" select="string(amount/@currency)"/><xsl:value-of select="amount"/></total>
    </xsl:element>
  </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

Principal output (no secondary output):

```xml
<receipt id="INV-2048"><customer>Ada & Co</customer><total currency="EUR">125.50</total></receipt>
```

Complete [empty-customer input](../examples/computed-xpath-constructors/empty.xml):

```xml
<invoice id="INV-EMPTY"><customer/><amount currency="EUR">0.00</amount></invoice>
```

Output:

```xml
<receipt id="INV-EMPTY"><customer/><total currency="EUR">0.00</total></receipt>
```

### Existing XQuery evidence

The existing `XQuery_ComputedElement_ComputedNameAndAtomicContent` test evaluates:

```xquery
(name(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 }), string(element { "dyn" } { 1, 2, 3 }))
```

It asserts two string items, `dyn` and `1 2 3`, through `XQueryCompiler` and `XQueryContext`. This is named unit-test evidence, not a new XQuery manifest fixture or proof that XPath constructors work.

deferred/enclosing-modes.md.text:
Enclosing modes

Deferred — portable named-mode dispatch remains supported

## 1. Name and Classification **Enclosing modes — Deferred.** [REQ-118 tier-4 decision](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) records the deferral. This record documents the boundary without enabling nested declarations. Bosak baseline reviewed 2026-10-12: [revision d7cc935a](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/d7cc935a3690c767fc17b01b90de4105a7140bed), engine 1.1.2. External reference: [XSLT 4.0 enclosing modes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#enclosing-modes). Immutable review source: [QT4CG xslt.xml at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), section ID `enclosing-modes`. The source records issue 82 / PR 542 (2023-06-20). This review does not recover the historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Keep invoice export rules together and ensure line processing uses the export rule set, while an audit pass uses a different set of rules. ## 3. Also Known As Nested template-rule declarations within `xsl:mode`. This is not the same as an empty mode declaration, ordinary named modes, the dynamic current mode, or a lexical default mode. ## 4. History / Supersedes The draft groups matched rules inside a named mode declaration and makes that mode the local default. It restricts contained templates and external applicable rules. Bosak retains its deferral; ordinary top-level named-mode rules already provide dispatch without that enclosure/isolation contract. ## 5. Motivation An ERP export and an internal audit can process the same invoice nodes differently. A nested rule group would improve locality, but a consumer needs a supported way to retain the export mode when descending to invoice lines. The alternative makes the mode explicit and tests the consequences of omitting it. ## 6. Language Alignment | Form | Verified Bosak boundary | |---|---| | `xsl:mode` containing templates, version 3.0 or 4.0 | `XTSE0260` | | Empty named `xsl:mode` plus top-level matched rules | Supported in the complete 3.0 and 4.0 examples | | Explicit recursive mode | Retains export dispatch | | Recursive `mode="#current"` | Retains the dynamic active mode | | Omitted recursive mode | Uses lexical default; selects the unnamed line rule in the test | | Root lexical `default-mode` set to export | Omitted recursion uses export in the tested stylesheet | The draft's invalid enclosing forms have specific static diagnostics (XTSE4005, XTSE4010 and XTSE4015, among others). Bosak's probes encounter the earlier generic empty-element restriction instead. These fixtures are refusal evidence, not implementation of the draft's diagnostic matrix. ## 7. Applicability Use ordinary modes for separate export/audit passes. Keep mode declarations empty and matched rules at top level. Ordinary modes do not enforce that all applicable rules are defined in one enclosed group; imports, packages, precedence and additional rules need separate review. ## 8. Structure The unnamed entry rule applies invoice nodes in `erp:export`. The invoice rule emits id/currency, applies lines in export mode, then emits a separator. The line rule emits each SKU. A separate audit rule reports line counts. The two prefixes used in the namespace probe identify the same expanded mode name. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) requires `xsl:mode` to be empty through `EmptyXsltElementNames`, and collects top-level template rules with `root.Elements(...)`. [TransformEngine](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) maintains the active mode stack. [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) executes exact stylesheets and asserts output or error markers. ## 10. Collaborations `xsl:apply-templates`, named modes, `#current`, lexical `default-mode`, `count` and `reverse` support the complete report. Selection order and line order are preserved in the fixtures. No external I/O or secondary outputs are required. ## 11. Consequences Raising the stylesheet version does not make enclosing modes work in Bosak. Moving templates to top level is a practical dispatch alternative, not equivalent rule isolation. `#current` is dynamic; an omitted mode is lexical, so they are not interchangeable. The deliberate unnamed line rule exposes this distinction through `wrong/` output. Input IDs, currencies and SKUs are projected strings; this report is not a data validator. ## 12. Implementation The must-be-empty validation raises `XTSE0260` before nested rule collection or draft-specific enclosure checks. The nine refusal fixtures cover the ordinary enclosing shape, unnamed declaration, named/mode-bearing/missing-match child, conflicting default, external applicable rule and duplicate enclosure. They do not certify unused nested bodies or package override behavior. No compiler/runtime changes or gate promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic [batch input](../examples/enclosing-modes/input.xml): ```xml ``` Complete [refused 4.0 stylesheet](../examples/enclosing-modes/main-refusal4.xsl): ```xml ; ``` Observed outcome: `XTSE0260`. No export result is asserted for this failing case. ### Complete portable XSLT 3.0 alternative [Top-level named rules](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable3.xsl): ```xml ; ``` Principal text output: ```text INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/; ``` The [version 4.0 comparison](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable4.xsl) returns the same report. The [current-mode fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/current-mode.xsl) uses `#current` for line recursion and returns the same report despite a competing unnamed line rule. ### Omitted recursion mode boundary Complete [omitted-mode fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/omitted-recursion-mode.xsl): ```xml ; wrong/ ``` Output: ```text INV-2048:EUR:wrong/wrong/;INV-2049:USD:wrong/; ``` The [lexical default fixture](../examples/enclosing-modes/lexical-default-mode.xsl) sets the root `default-mode` to export and obtains the export report with omitted recursion. That is an explicit lexical policy, not enclosing-mode support. ### Empty and reordered input Complete empty input: ```xml ``` Output is the empty string (zero principal text bytes). Complete reordered input: ```xml ``` Output: ```text INV-2049:USD:P300/;INV-2048:EUR:P200/P100/; ``` The reverse-selection fixture reverses invoices without reversing their line sequence. The audit fixture reports `audit:INV-2048:2;audit:INV-2049:1;`, using its own top-level mode rules. ### Complete fixture inventory The [manifest](../examples/cases.json) executes 20 cases, including nine generic refusals and eleven successful mode/ordering comparisons. Errors assert compile/capture markers without promising a universal detection stage. | Fixture | Mode | Exact output/error marker | |---|---|---| | [main-refusal4](../examples/enclosing-modes/main-refusal4.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [main-refusal3](../examples/enclosing-modes/main-refusal3.xsl) | xslt31 | `XTSE0260` | | [unnamed](../examples/enclosing-modes/unnamed.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [named-child](../examples/enclosing-modes/named-child.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [explicit-child-mode](../examples/enclosing-modes/explicit-child-mode.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [missing-child-match](../examples/enclosing-modes/missing-child-match.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [default-conflict](../examples/enclosing-modes/default-conflict.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [external-rule](../examples/enclosing-modes/external-rule.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [duplicate](../examples/enclosing-modes/duplicate.xsl) | xslt40 | `XTSE0260` | | [portable3](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable3.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;` | | [portable4](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable4.xsl) | xslt40 | `INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;` | | [portable-empty](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable-empty.xsl) | xslt31 | `` | | [portable-reordered](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable-reordered.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2049:USD:P300/;INV-2048:EUR:P200/P100/;` | | [portable-reverse](../examples/enclosing-modes/portable-reverse.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2049:USD:P300/;INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;` | | [audit](../examples/enclosing-modes/audit.xsl) | xslt31 | `audit:INV-2048:2;audit:INV-2049:1;` | | [current-mode](../examples/enclosing-modes/current-mode.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;` | | [omitted-recursion-mode](../examples/enclosing-modes/omitted-recursion-mode.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:EUR:wrong/wrong/;INV-2049:USD:wrong/;` | | [lexical-default-mode](../examples/enclosing-modes/lexical-default-mode.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;` | | [namespace-alias](../examples/enclosing-modes/namespace-alias.xsl) | xslt31 | `INV-2048:EUR:P100/P200/;INV-2049:USD:P300/;` | | [empty-declaration](../examples/enclosing-modes/empty-declaration.xsl) | xslt40 | `ready` | ## 14. Performance Export visits the selected invoices and their lines; audit counts selected line children. No benchmark or performance claim for deferred enclosing modes is made. ## 15. Known Uses This ERP export/audit is synthetic integration evidence. [StylesheetTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/StylesheetTests.cs) includes `Hash_Current_Resolves_To_Current_Mode`, `Mode_All_Matches_All_Modes`, `Mode_OnNoMatch_ShallowSkip` and `Initial_Mode_With_Source_Succeeds` for ordinary mode behavior. [ModeConflictResolutionTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ModeConflictResolutionTests.cs) includes `SamePrecedenceConflict_UnresolvedByHigherPrecedence_ThrowsXtse0545` and `SamePrecedenceDisjointAttributes_MergeWithoutError`. These tests are not enclosing-mode conformance evidence. No conformance gate membership changes are included. ## 16. Related Features [Computed XPath constructors](computed-node-constructors.md), [named XSLT item types](xslt-item-type.md), [named XSLT record types](xslt-record-type.md), [completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) and [supplementary audit](../SUPPLEMENTARY-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md).
