xsl:item-type: published alias boundaries

21 October 2026

## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT4.0 surface in public1.23.2; complete declaration contract not certified.** This existing path is retained for links; deferred describes its historical dossier, not all present behavior. [Current pinned review](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Give an existing permitted type a stylesheet-context name without inventing a new nominal record identity. ## 3. Also Known As Named item-type alias; enumeration or structural-record alias in the reviewed forms. It does not itself request a generated constructor. ## 4. History / Supersedes The earlier REQ-118 deferral and1.2.0 implementation logs remain in the [historical snapshot](../../history/REQ126-ITEM-TYPE-SNAPSHOT-20261021.md). Enumeration-alias delivery isf53bc80f; structural-record aliases are669c862a. Current review provenance does not reconstruct the original adopted draft or promote every deferred declaration contract. ## 5. Motivation An intake classifier can name an integer quantity or permitted status set, while keeping validation and routing policy visible. ## 6. Language Alignment An alias is not a C# nominal class. Instance-of tests the supplied value; an XSLT @as binding can first perform conversion. Identical textual values or fields do not imply every type check agrees. ## 7. Applicability Use only the declared/verified aliases in a supporting host. Use ordinary3.1 types and explicit predicates in a portable3.0 stylesheet. ## 8. Structure Example declarations: `xsl:item-type name="t:status" as="enum('ready','queued')"` and `name="t:shape" as="record(x as xs:integer)"`. These are descriptive reviewed forms, not a complete grammar. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs), the XPath type system and the compiled stylesheet context resolve names. No new public registration API is introduced here. ## 10. Collaborations Combine aliases with bindings and type/pattern checks; compare the [intake report](../examples/intake-types/README.md) and [record identity reference](xslt-record-type.md). ## 11. Consequences Reduces repeated type syntax but adds a host/context dependency. Expanded names matter; enum treat mismatch raises XPDY0050. Do not treat successful coercion as evidence that an unconverted map already carried an annotation. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [structural-binding.xsl](../examples/intake-types/structural-binding.xsl) returns true|false for converted versus original map. [enum-allowed](../examples/intake-types/enum-allowed.xsl) and [enum-rejected](../examples/intake-types/enum-rejected.xsl) distinguish allowed values. The complete report has normal, empty and reordered cases. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses [Xslt40ItemTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ItemTypeTests.cs) and [Xslt40StructuralRecordAliasTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40StructuralRecordAliasTests.cs); new intake-types enum/alias/structural rows. Missing @as and duplicates are explicit diagnostic controls. No new GatedSets membership; AC-03 remains partial. ## 16. Related Features [Structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [enums](../type-system/enum-types.md), [type/pattern grammar](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md), [pattern entry](../xslt-instructions/structured-value-patterns.md).

deferred/xslt-record-type.md.text:
xsl:record-type: construction and identity

21 October 2026

**REQ-126 C03 complete — 26 October 2026:** [Constructor/type review](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles eight entries and all 49 focus constructors. All 1,333 asserted controls match across 1,357 observations; 245 focused schema/API/host tests pass. Bounded nominal defaults/static fields are now evidenced. Generic wide casts, decimal precision, schema/host context and broader conversion remain explicit boundaries; C02's atomic-annotation defect remains open. Ten closure workpackages remain; C04 is next. No engine/test/example/version/gate change or acceptance waiver; skips/Braid/extension work stays deferred. Earlier checkpoint counts are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT4.0 named-record behavior in public1.23.2; broader contracts remain separately scoped.** The historical deferred URL is retained. [Current review](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) separates constructor identity, structural annotation and noncoercing type/pattern tests. ## 2. Intent Establish a stylesheet-declared record identity and, when requested, a generated constructor. ## 3. Also Known As Named or nominative record type. This is distinct from an anonymous structural record alias and from ordinary map key equality. ## 4. History / Supersedes The old deferral/source1.2.0 snapshot and accumulated implementation notes are [preserved separately](../../history/REQ126-RECORD-TYPE-SNAPSHOT-20261021.md). Current source evidence includes named record pattern delivery2244c1d7. No complete draft adoption or feature-tier promotion is inferred from this bounded update. ## 5. Motivation Two intake interfaces can use the same field names while needing different record identities. Constructors and type checks must distinguish them. ## 6. Language Alignment Matching fields do not make t:point and t:other nominally identical. A plain map is not automatically a t:point in an instance-of or record pattern test. Conversion in a binding/function call is a separate contract, not a contradiction of that result. ## 7. Applicability Use the declared constructor and tested compiled stylesheet context when named identity is required. Use portable maps and explicit predicates when the receiving processor lacks these declarations. ## 8. Structure ``; the complete namespaces are in [nominal-own.xsl](../examples/intake-types/nominal-own.xsl). constructor="no" does not generate the called function. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) registers the declarations/constructors; [RecordPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/RecordPattern.cs) tests existing values. Keep declaration/type/pattern positions distinct. ## 10. Collaborations Named records can be tested by named type/record patterns. [xsl:item-type](xslt-item-type.md) may name a structural shape without creating this nominal identity. ## 11. Consequences Preserves an identity boundary beyond fields but adds declaration/context coupling. This review does not certify every recursive/default/static/visibility/import/package/error edge, nor a standalone XPath named-declaration language. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [nominal-own](../examples/intake-types/nominal-own.xsl) returns true, [nominal-other](../examples/intake-types/nominal-other.xsl) and [nominal-plain-map](../examples/intake-types/nominal-plain-map.xsl) return false. [nominal-no-constructor](../examples/intake-types/nominal-no-constructor.xsl) intentionally raises XPST0017. No external variables/resources are required. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses [Xslt40RecordPatternTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40RecordPatternTests.cs) and [Xslt40TypePatternTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40TypePatternTests.cs); new intake-types nominal/type-nominal rows. Applicable XSLT evidence is separate from XPath qt4tests gate membership; AC-03 is not waived. ## 16. experimental/fn-scan.md.text:
fn:scan

Catalog entry — Functions · Experimental

**C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **`fn:scan`** — **Experimental** (ships only at the `XPath40Experimental` level; static XPST0017 at both `XPath31` *and* frozen `XPath40`). Spec: F&O 4.0 §2.5.15, added by qt4cg Issue 2823 / PR 2824 (31 July 2026). Landed: REQ-123 S1 (1.1.0 track), level-plumbing slice 2026-10-09. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [F&O 4.0: fn:scan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-scan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. Draft evolution: [QT4CG PR #2824](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/2824) records the scan proposal referenced by the adoption dossier. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #98](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/98), [immutable mainline revision `bd18e42f`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/bd18e42f33b5e69817f059f6429f4b08e639a5a3) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Return every intermediate accumulator of a left fold as a **sequence of single-member arrays**: `fn:scan($input, $init, $action)` yields `[$init]`, then `[$action($acc, $item, $pos)]` for each input item — N input items produce N+1 arrays. There is no additional outer array. ## 3. Also Known As "Prefix scan", "running fold". **Do not implement** `scan-left` / `scan-right`: those names never existed in the accepted draft — the pair was consolidated into the single left-fold `fn:scan` before stabilization (see [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) for the sibling rename story). ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes hand-threaded accumulation of intermediate states in 3.1. The [complete stock-ledger baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) uses `fold-left` and `array:append`; the [experimental case](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath) uses `fn:scan`. Both display `100,120,85,95` for an opening stock of 100 units and movements of +20, -35, and +10. | Before (3.1) | After (4.0-Exp) | |---|---| | `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` | ## 5. Motivation Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison. ## 6. Language Alignment Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback. ## 7. Applicability Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state. Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move. ## 8. Structure ``` fn:scan(input as item()*, init as item()*, action as fn(*)) as array(*)* ``` ## 9. Participants - `FunctionLibrary` — experimental-only signature template (`IsXPath40ExperimentalOnly`), invisible to `fn:function-lookup` / dynamic dispatch below the experimental level. - `EvaluationContext.IsXPath40Experimental` — runtime level flag. - Version gate (`XPath31Expression`) — static XPST0017 in call form *and* named-function-ref form at both lower levels. ## 10. Collaborations - The **experimental level plumbing** (REQ-123 S1) is the collaboration that matters: `fn:scan` was the first function gated exclusively to `XPath40Experimental`, and it established the template every later experimental addition follows (dedicated signature templates, lookup invisibility, call+ref static errors). - Destructuring `let` ([destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md)) is the natural consumer of each emitted single-member array's shape in surrounding code. ## 11. Consequences Benefits: direct expression of all intermediate states; the callback position parameter enables position-aware accumulations. Retaining the history requires storage for its states; no constant-memory guarantee is implied. Liabilities: **experimental-tier semantics may change as the draft moves** — the N+1 / single-member-array shape is precisely the kind of detail a WG review adjusts. Pin your usage to a Bosak version and re-run the qt4tests `fn-scan` set (if promoted by then) on upgrades. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-scan. scan is Experimental-only in calls and lookup, with N+1 single-member-array states and empty input retaining the seed. Its existing gate retry is not frozen API promotion. No new function syntax or frozen promotion. C02 callback semantics and C06 host/profile ownership remain distinct from membership in GatedSets. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles N+1 accumulator states retain single-member array boundaries; Empty input retains the initial state; Position-aware callback; Experimental-only availability. **Boundaries:** No frozen-profile adoption or constant-memory guarantee; generic function coercion beyond verified callbacks is not certified. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs` (experimental signature + implementation), `src/Bosak.XPath.Api/XPath31Expression.cs` (experimental-aware static gate), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (`IsXPath40Experimental`). Version gate: XPST0017 at `XPath31` **and** `XPath40`; legal only at `XPath40Experimental`. Unit evidence: experimental-level tests in `Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests` (see REQ-123 S1). ## 13. Sample Code Practical case: [stock ledger](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath). The [empty-movement case](../examples/fn-scan/edge.xpath) returns only the opening balance, displayed as `100`. Both cases require `XPath40Experimental`; the [earlier baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) runs at `XPath31`. ~~~xquery fn:scan((1, 2, 3), 0, fn($acc, $it) { $acc + $it }) (: → [0], [1], [3], [6] — every running total, init first :) fn:scan((), "start", fn($acc, $it) { $acc || $it }) (: → ["start"] — empty input yields just the init :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Implementation expectation: one callback per input item and one wrapper array per retained state. Accumulator size can dominate storage and callback cost. No measured comparison against the 3.1 array-append baseline is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses Published examples: `fn-scan-main`, `fn-scan-edge`, `fn-scan-before` in `CatalogExampleTests`. The successful experimental cases also verify refusal at both lower compatibility levels. This is example evidence, separate from gate status. qt4tests set `fn-scan` is promoted into `GatedSets` in [ConformanceRunner40](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). The 1.1.0 gate run records 11 experimental-level passes and zero gated failures. Gate membership does not move the function into the frozen compatibility tier; its successful examples still require `XPath40Experimental`. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Evaluate_Scan_XPath40Experimental_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-scan`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) — the sibling "consolidated/renamed before stabilization" story. - [destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md) — frozen-tier contrast from the same delivery wave. - [method-call-operator.md](../operators-and-syntax/method-call-operator.md) — another post-June-2026 deferred surface. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold).*

|---|---|
| `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` |
sections.5:
Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every
intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses
the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison.
sections.6: Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback.
sections.7:
Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state.

Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move.
sections.8:
```
fn:scan(input as item()*, init as item()*, action as fn(*)) as array(*)*
```
sections.9:
- `FunctionLibrary` — experimental-only signature template (`IsXPath40ExperimentalOnly`), invisible to `fn:function-lookup` / dynamic dispatch below the experimental level.
- `EvaluationContext.IsXPath40Experimental` — runtime level flag.
- Version gate (`XPath31Expression`) — static XPST0017 in call form *and* named-function-ref form at both lower levels.
sections.10:
- The **experimental level plumbing** (REQ-123 S1) is the collaboration that matters: `fn:scan` was the first function gated exclusively to `XPath40Experimental`, and it established the template every later experimental addition follows (dedicated signature templates, lookup invisibility, call+ref static errors).
- Destructuring `let` ([destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md)) is the natural consumer of each emitted single-member array's shape in surrounding code.
sections.11:
Benefits: direct expression of all intermediate states; the callback position
parameter enables position-aware accumulations. Retaining the history requires
storage for its states; no constant-memory guarantee is implied.

Liabilities: **experimental-tier semantics may change as the draft moves** — the N+1 / single-member-array shape is precisely the kind of detail a WG review adjusts. Pin your usage to a Bosak version and re-run the qt4tests `fn-scan` set (if promoted by then) on upgrades.
sections.12:
**C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-scan. scan is Experimental-only in calls and lookup, with N+1 single-member-array states and empty input retaining the seed. Its existing gate retry is not frozen API promotion. No new function syntax or frozen promotion. C02 callback semantics and C06 host/profile ownership remain distinct from membership in GatedSets. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance.


**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles N+1 accumulator states retain single-member array boundaries; Empty input retains the initial state; Position-aware callback; Experimental-only availability. **Boundaries:** No frozen-profile adoption or constant-memory guarantee; generic function coercion beyond verified callbacks is not certified. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance.

Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs` (experimental signature + implementation), `src/Bosak.XPath.Api/XPath31Expression.cs` (experimental-aware static gate), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (`IsXPath40Experimental`). Version gate: XPST0017 at `XPath31` **and** `XPath40`; legal only at `XPath40Experimental`. Unit evidence: experimental-level tests in `Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests` (see REQ-123 S1).
sections.13:
Practical case: [stock ledger](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath). The
[empty-movement case](../examples/fn-scan/edge.xpath) returns only the opening
balance, displayed as `100`. Both cases require `XPath40Experimental`; the
[earlier baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) runs at `XPath31`.

~~~xquery
fn:scan((1, 2, 3), 0, fn($acc, $it) { $acc + $it })
  (: → [0], [1], [3], [6] — every running total, init first :)

fn:scan((), "start", fn($acc, $it) { $acc || $it })
  (: → ["start"] — empty input yields just the init :)
~~~
sections.14:
Implementation expectation: one callback per input item and one wrapper array
per retained state. Accumulator size can dominate storage and callback cost.
No measured comparison against the 3.1 array-append baseline is claimed.
sections.15:
Published examples: `fn-scan-main`, `fn-scan-edge`, `fn-scan-before` in
`CatalogExampleTests`. The successful experimental cases also verify refusal at
both lower compatibility levels. This is example evidence, separate from gate status.

qt4tests set `fn-scan` is promoted into `GatedSets` in
[ConformanceRunner40](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs).
The 1.1.0 gate run records 11 experimental-level passes and zero gated failures.
Gate membership does not move the function into the frozen compatibility tier;
its successful examples still require `XPath40Experimental`.

functions/atomic-equal.md.text:
Atomic equality

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Atomic equality** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:atomic-equal](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-atomic-equal). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #108](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/108), [immutable mainline revision `cbf7f88c`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cbf7f88ce8364334040a819f96967622992f24a2) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use type-specific comparisons and deliberate NaN handling. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/atomic-equal/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/atomic-equal/main.xpath). Both yield `true` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A telemetry feed uses NaN for unavailable measurements and compares two snapshots. Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:atomic-equal(xs:double('NaN'), xs:double('NaN')) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Atomic equality distinguishes value-family policy and NaN; Atomic input/type errors remain distinct from deep node/map equality. **Boundaries:** Representative atomic families only; do not generalize the sample to structural equality or every derived atomic type. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/atomic-equal/main.xpath) yields `true`. The [edge case](../examples/atomic-equal/edge.xpath) yields `false`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: small scalar comparison overhead, including atomic type classification. It does not traverse a document tree. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `atomic-equal-main`, `atomic-equal-edge`, `atomic-equal-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_AtomicEqual_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0017`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_AtomicEqual_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-atomic-equal`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/batch-extrema.md.text:
Batch Extrema and Component Codes

Frozen 4.0 — changed existing-function contracts and observed limits

## 1. Name and Classification [fn:min](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-min) and [fn:max](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-max) already exist in XPath 3.1. Their changed 4.0 contracts are outside the 117-name inventory of 4.0-only functions. Bosak's QName extension was delivered in [PR #114](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/114), [33894747](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/33894747f04da970a1f3c0f17fa960fa1f620605). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review does not recover the historical adopted draft. ## 2. Intent Report a quality-control batch's accepted decimal range and the endpoints of its namespace-aware component-code inventory. Preserve rejected row identifiers and make empty batches explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Minimum, maximum and extrema describe these functions. Component-code endpoints are namespace/local-name ordering, not a severity ranking or business priority. ## 4. History / Supersedes The stable [3.1 min](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-min) and [3.1 max](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-max) contracts use numeric promotion and a narrower set of orderable types. The reviewed 4.0 draft compares converted values through the broader `fn:compare` ordering and returns a selected converted input value. Bosak adds QName extrema, but its shared numeric and duration paths retain earlier behavior. The 3.1 report below uses explicit namespace/local-name folds instead of calling extrema on QNames. ## 5. Motivation Imported readings need a useful range without allowing malformed values to silently become NaN. Namespaced component codes also need a deterministic index boundary independent of the XML prefix chosen by a sender. Both tasks benefit from explicit conversion and ordering policies. ## 6. Language Alignment Bosak registers one- and two-argument forms of both functions. Empty input returns an empty sequence. Untyped atomic values are converted to doubles; explicitly supplied strings remain strings. Thus untyped XML numbers `2` and `10` have a numeric range, while string values `'2'` and `'10'` have a lexical range. Numeric NaN contaminates either extreme; the application must screen it when missing measurements should be excluded. Mixing number and string raises `FORG0006` in these fixtures. QNames are ordered by namespace URI and then local name in codepoint order. Prefixes do not determine ordering. Equivalent QNames may carry different prefixes, so the report prints expanded names rather than asserting a chosen prefix. The draft leaves the chosen representative of equal extrema unspecified. The second argument selects string collation. Bosak accepts the demonstrated empty-collation form in both profiles; only the 4.0 draft's default-on-empty contract is claimed. Keyword `values` matches the reviewed parameter name and requires 4.0 syntax. **Observed contract gaps:** mixed numeric values are still promoted in Bosak. `min((3.1, 3.1e0))` produces a double whose exact comparison with decimal `3.1` is `1`; under the pinned draft's ordering the minimum is the decimal and that comparison should be `0`. The equal-highest integer/float example produces a double even though that converted input value is not the selected extreme. The integer/decimal probe also returns a decimal rather than preserving the winning integer. Plain durations remain refused with `FORG0006`, although the reviewed atomic comparator defines their ordering. Fixtures marked `observed` record these limits; they are not conforming-result assertions. When an engine correction lands, update those observed expectations and retain the historical behavior and migration note alongside the corrected contract. ## 7. Applicability The synthetic quality-control vocabulary is not an industry schema. IDs and component-code text are assumed present, with resolvable namespace prefixes. `castable as xs:decimal` screens malformed, absent and NaN value text. It does not validate units, sensor calibration, engineering tolerances or business ranges. An invalid QName or undeclared prefix requires separate validation. The host owns data acquisition and corrective action. ## 8. Structure Split accepted/rejected rows, explicitly convert accepted values to decimals, resolve every row's component code in its XML namespace context, and calculate numeric extrema plus code endpoints. Codes include rejected readings so the inventory describes the full imported batch, while the numeric range uses only accepted rows. ## 9. Participants Readings carry values, IDs and code names. Decimal constructors implement the numeric policy. `resolve-QName` creates namespace-aware codes. Extrema choose boundaries. A label function formats expanded names without prefix dependence. ## 10. Collaborations Every accepted value becomes a decimal before aggregation, avoiding the mixed numeric promotion gap in this report. An empty range or code inventory prints `-`; zero remains a real measurement. The 3.1 code comparator compares namespace URIs first and local names second with explicit codepoint collation. Two folds retain first and last endpoints without constructing an ambiguous combined key. ## 11. Consequences Both reports agree on this deliberately normalized decimal/QName workflow. That agreement does not establish mixed-type equivalence between the language versions. The endpoints organize a code inventory and have no severity meaning. Malformed values remain traceable; the decimal storage precision limit and unvalidated code/unit/range constraints remain outside the demonstrated contract. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Empty input, atomization, numeric/string and QName extrema; Omitted/empty collation and values keyword; NaN contamination and incomparable-family errors. **Boundaries:** Use homogeneous validated atomic inputs and explicit collation; remaining coercion/mixed-family combinations require targeted review. Follow-up groups: F06, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for QName extrema and keyword calls. The numeric baseline runs with `Compatibility31` and its QName endpoints use folds. Default 3.1 numeric/string extrema remain available, while these nonempty QName extrema fail during evaluation with `FORG0006`. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers. `baselineExpected` checks shared default-mode results; `baselineError` checks the declared default compile/evaluation error. The observed gap cases are explicitly labeled rather than presented as complete draft conformance. This delivery changes neither the engine nor gate membership. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` ### XPath 4.0 report [Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/main.xpath): ```xpath let $rows := parse-xml('')/batch/reading return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal] return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)] return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.) return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .) return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) } return let $first := min($codes) return let $last := max($codes) return let $low := min($values) return let $high := max($values) return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last)) ``` Exact output: ```text accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing ``` A, B and C supply valid decimals; D and E remain rejected identifiers. The ERP namespace sorts before the QA namespace; within QA, `missing` is the last local name. This explains the code endpoints without assigning a business rank. ### XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $rows := parse-xml('')/batch/reading return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal] return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)] return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.) return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .) return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) } return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint' return let $less := function($a, $b) { let $ns := compare(namespace-uri-from-QName($a), namespace-uri-from-QName($b), $cp) return if ($ns eq 0) then compare(local-name-from-QName($a), local-name-from-QName($b), $cp) lt 0 else $ns lt 0 } return let $first := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($next, $best)) then $next else $best }) return let $last := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($best, $next)) then $next else $best }) return let $low := min($values) return let $high := max($values) return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last)) ``` Exact output: ```text accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing ``` The fold comparator performs two comparisons, preserving the namespace/local-name ordering even when one namespace URI is a prefix of another. The numeric part uses the same explicit decimal normalization policy as the 4.0 report. ### Complete fixture inventory | Runnable case | Mode | Exact result/error marker | Default 3.1 outcome also sections.1:
[fn:min](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-min)
and [fn:max](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-max)
already exist in XPath 3.1. Their changed 4.0 contracts are outside the
117-name inventory of 4.0-only functions. Bosak's QName extension was delivered
in [PR #114](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/114),
[33894747](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/33894747f04da970a1f3c0f17fa960fa1f620605).
Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable
[QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml).
This review does not recover the historical adopted draft.
sections.2:
Report a quality-control batch's accepted decimal range and the endpoints of its
namespace-aware component-code inventory. Preserve rejected row identifiers and
make empty batches explicit.
sections.3:
Minimum, maximum and extrema describe these functions. Component-code endpoints
are namespace/local-name ordering, not a severity ranking or business priority.
sections.4:
The stable [3.1 min](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-min) and
[3.1 max](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-max) contracts use numeric
promotion and a narrower set of orderable types. The reviewed 4.0 draft compares
converted values through the broader `fn:compare` ordering and returns a selected
converted input value. Bosak adds QName extrema, but its shared numeric and
duration paths retain earlier behavior. The 3.1 report below uses explicit
namespace/local-name folds instead of calling extrema on QNames.
sections.5:
Imported readings need a useful range without allowing malformed values to
silently become NaN. Namespaced component codes also need a deterministic index
boundary independent of the XML prefix chosen by a sender. Both tasks benefit
from explicit conversion and ordering policies.
sections.6:
Bosak registers one- and two-argument forms of both functions. Empty input returns
an empty sequence. Untyped atomic values are converted to doubles; explicitly
supplied strings remain strings. Thus untyped XML numbers `2` and `10` have a
numeric range, while string values `'2'` and `'10'` have a lexical range.
Numeric NaN contaminates either extreme; the application must screen it when
missing measurements should be excluded. Mixing number and string raises
`FORG0006` in these fixtures.

QNames are ordered by namespace URI and then local name in codepoint order.
Prefixes do not determine ordering. Equivalent QNames may carry different
prefixes, so the report prints expanded names rather than asserting a chosen
prefix. The draft leaves the chosen representative of equal extrema unspecified.

The second argument selects string collation. Bosak accepts the demonstrated
empty-collation form in both profiles; only the 4.0 draft's default-on-empty
contract is claimed. Keyword `values` matches the reviewed parameter name and
requires 4.0 syntax.

**Observed contract gaps:** mixed numeric values are still promoted in Bosak.
`min((3.1, 3.1e0))` produces a double whose exact comparison with decimal `3.1`
is `1`; under the pinned draft's ordering the minimum is the decimal and that
comparison should be `0`. The equal-highest integer/float example produces a
double even though that converted input value is not the selected extreme.
The integer/decimal probe also returns a decimal rather than preserving the
winning integer. Plain durations remain refused with `FORG0006`, although the
reviewed atomic comparator defines their ordering. Fixtures marked `observed`
record these limits; they are not conforming-result assertions.
When an engine correction lands, update those observed expectations and retain
the historical behavior and migration note alongside the corrected contract.
sections.7:
The synthetic quality-control vocabulary is not an industry schema. IDs and
component-code text are assumed present, with resolvable namespace prefixes.
`castable as xs:decimal` screens malformed, absent and NaN value text. It does not
validate units, sensor calibration, engineering tolerances or business ranges.
An invalid QName or undeclared prefix requires separate validation. The host owns
data acquisition and corrective action.
sections.8:
Split accepted/rejected rows, explicitly convert accepted values to decimals,
resolve every row's component code in its XML namespace context, and calculate
numeric extrema plus code endpoints. Codes include rejected readings so the
inventory describes the full imported batch, while the numeric range uses only
accepted rows.
sections.9:
Readings carry values, IDs and code names. Decimal constructors implement the
numeric policy. `resolve-QName` creates namespace-aware codes. Extrema choose
boundaries. A label function formats expanded names without prefix dependence.
sections.10:
Every accepted value becomes a decimal before aggregation, avoiding the mixed
numeric promotion gap in this report. An empty range or code inventory prints
`-`; zero remains a real measurement. The 3.1 code comparator compares namespace
URIs first and local names second with explicit codepoint collation. Two folds
retain first and last endpoints without constructing an ambiguous combined key.
sections.11:
Both reports agree on this deliberately normalized decimal/QName workflow.
That agreement does not establish mixed-type equivalence between the language
versions. The endpoints organize a code inventory and have no severity meaning.
Malformed values remain traceable; the decimal storage precision limit and
unvalidated code/unit/range constraints remain outside the demonstrated contract.
sections.12:
**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Empty input, atomization, numeric/string and QName extrema; Omitted/empty collation and values keyword; NaN contamination and incomparable-family errors. **Boundaries:** Use homogeneous validated atomic inputs and explicit collation; remaining coercion/mixed-family combinations require targeted review. Follow-up groups: F06, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance.

Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for QName extrema and keyword calls.
The numeric baseline runs with `Compatibility31` and its QName endpoints use
folds. Default 3.1 numeric/string extrema remain available, while these nonempty
QName extrema fail during evaluation with `FORG0006`.

The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs)
verifies exact text/error markers. `baselineExpected` checks shared default-mode
results; `baselineError` checks the declared default compile/evaluation error.
The observed gap cases are explicitly labeled rather than presented as complete
draft conformance. This delivery changes neither the engine nor gate membership.
sections.13:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>
```

### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>')/batch/reading
return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $first := min($codes)
return let $last := max($codes)
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

Exact output:

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

A, B and C supply valid decimals; D and E remain rejected identifiers. The ERP
namespace sorts before the QA namespace; within QA, `missing` is the last local
name. This explains the code endpoints without assigning a business rank.

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>')/batch/reading
return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return let $less := function($a, $b) {
  let $ns := compare(namespace-uri-from-QName($a), namespace-uri-from-QName($b), $cp)
  return if ($ns eq 0) then compare(local-name-from-QName($a), local-name-from-QName($b), $cp) lt 0 else $ns lt 0
}
return let $first := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($next, $best)) then $next else $best })
return let $last := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($best, $next)) then $next else $best })
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

Exact output:

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

The fold comparator performs two comparisons, preserving the namespace/local-name
ordering even when one namespace URI is a prefix of another. The numeric part
uses the same explicit decimal normalization policy as the 4.0 report.

functions/bounded-retries.md.text:
Bounded Retry State

Frozen 4.0 — precondition and postcondition loops with an attempt budget

## 1. Name and Classification **Bounded retry state — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:while-do](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-while-do) and [fn:do-until](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-do-until). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Advance an invoice-submission state until it is accepted or its attempt budget is consumed. Keep the status, attempt count and response history visible in the result so acceptance can be distinguished from budget exhaustion. ## 3. Also Known As Precondition loop (`while-do`) and postcondition loop (`do-until`). These are explanatory terms, not alternative function names. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can carry state through a bounded `fold-left`, skipping updates after acceptance. The complete comparison below returns the same report for the illustrated responses. It still visits every position in the fixed range; it is not a general early-terminating loop. Recursive helper functions are another option in a host language that supports named function declarations. ## 5. Motivation Electronic invoice gateways commonly acknowledge a submission before later reporting acceptance. An application must stop checking once accepted and must also stop when its configured attempt budget is used. Treating exhausted attempts as success would hide invoices still awaiting acceptance. The fixture uses recorded responses to make that state transition reproducible. ## 6. Language Alignment `while-do($input, $predicate, $action)` tests the current value before updating it. False or empty returns that value immediately; true calls the action and repeats with the new value. Position starts at one and increments after an action. `do-until($input, $action, $predicate)` always calls the action first, then tests its new value using the same position. True returns it; false or empty repeats at the next position. Note the opposite meanings of a true predicate and the opposite callback argument order. Both callbacks receive the **whole current `item()*` value**, not individual members of a sequence. Actions may return any sequence, including empty. The examples use two-argument inline functions to show both state and position explicitly. ## 7. Applicability Use for repeated pure state transformations with a clear stopping condition. The sample assumes a nonnegative integer attempt limit, starts attempts at zero, and recognizes only `accepted` as success. Missing response/status is normalized to `pending`; other statuses remain unsuccessful and consume the budget. A production integration should separately classify permanent rejection and validate gateway responses according to its own protocol. The XPath consumes an already supplied response fixture. The host application owns actual requests, idempotency keys, persistence, timeouts, delays and any backoff policy. Here an attempt means one recorded status check; it does not mean resubmitting the invoice. No network request or sleep occurs in the expression. ## 8. Structure A state map contains `attempts`, `status` and a sequence-valued `trace`. The action reads the response at the current one-based position and constructs a replacement map. The predicate combines status with the finite attempt limit. The final report exposes acceptance or exhaustion independently. ## 9. Participants The submission fixture provides ordered responses. The initial state supplies an empty trace and zero attempts. The action advances state. The predicate owns the stopping rule. The report presents the final state for the caller. ## 10. Collaborations For `while-do`, continue while not accepted **and** below the limit. For `do-until`, stop when accepted **or** at the limit. An outer zero-budget guard is essential for `do-until`, because the function itself always runs its action. The initially-accepted cases show why replacing one form with the other can change behavior: `while-do` does nothing, whereas `do-until` performs a new check. ## 11. Consequences A finite budget plus an action that increments attempts guarantees termination for these fixtures, even if no response ever reports acceptance. The loops have no implicit maximum iteration count or delay. An unchanged state with a predicate that never stops could run indefinitely; every runnable case here has a bound or a predicate that terminates on its first call. Exceptions propagate; the functions do not automatically convert them into retryable outcomes. ## 12. reporting acceptance. An application must stop checking once accepted and must

attempts as success would hide invoices still awaiting acceptance.

Complete synthetic input: a gateway status-check sequence for invoice INV-2048.
The third response remains unread because the second response is accepted.

```xml
<submission id="INV-2048">
  <response status="pending"/>
  <response status="accepted"/>
  <response status="pending"/>
</submission>
```

### Test before the action

[Runnable while-do expression](../examples/bounded-retries/while-main.xpath):

```xpath
let $responses := parse-xml('<submission id="INV-2048"><response status="pending"/><response status="accepted"/><response status="pending"/></submission>')/submission/response
let $limit := 3
let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()}
let $advance := function($state, $position) {
  let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1])
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
let $final := while-do($initial, function($state, $position) { $state?status ne 'accepted' and $state?attempts lt $limit }, $advance)

```

```

functions/configured-label-callbacks.md.text:
Configured Label Callbacks

Frozen 4.0 — bind policy arguments and pass through unchanged values

## 1. Name and Classification **Configured label callbacks — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:partial-apply](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-partial-apply) and [fn:identity](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-identity). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. The original identity registration follow-up is [eedcb321](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/eedcb321848ff7e9381c34fd72cb42db4994992f). ## 2. Intent Configure a shipping-label formatter once by binding its prefix and case policy, then reuse the resulting one-argument callback for every customer name. Use an identity callback when already formatted labels should pass through unchanged. ## 3. Also Known As Argument binding and a pass-through callback describe the two operations. They introduce no function aliases. Partial application binds selected arguments; it does not execute the formatter at binding time. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 supports placeholder partial application: `$format('SHIP: ', ?, true())`. The complete comparison below produces the same callback and report. The 4.0 function accepts a runtime map of argument positions without requiring a statically known arity, and can bind every argument to produce a zero-argument function. The earlier identity equivalent is `function($value) { $value }`. ## 5. Motivation A dispatch batch can share a label prefix and capitalization rule while each record supplies a different name. Passing all configuration arguments on every call obscures that fixed policy. Binding policy values exposes a simple callback that fits `for-each`. An identity callback lets the same processing stage accept already formatted labels without changing their content. ## 6. Language Alignment `partial-apply($function, $arguments)` takes a callable and a map with positive integer keys identifying **one-based** argument positions. Unbound parameters retain their original relative order. Binding all parameters gives arity zero; an empty map returns the original callable. Keys beyond the function's arity are ignored, rather than reporting a misspelled configuration position. String, zero and negative keys raise XPTY0004 in the demonstrated cases. Maps and arrays are callable too, and can have their single lookup argument bound. Supplied values undergo function conversion when parameter metadata permits. Some Bosak built-ins lack that metadata; their conversion errors may surface when the resulting function is invoked. The bound-type-error fixture exercises that call, rather than claiming all validation happens eagerly. `identity($input)` returns the same `item()*` value, including an empty sequence, a whole sequence or a container. For nodes it preserves identity, rather than copying. `identity#1` supplies a function item where a callback is required. ## 7. Applicability Use for reusable callbacks configured by runtime policy, or for binding all arguments into a deferred zero-argument call. A fixed, statically known function may be clearer with 3.1 placeholders. Validate configuration positions separately if silently ignored high keys would hide errors. The label case assumes nonempty customer names validated upstream. It normalizes whitespace and applies a simple uppercase policy; it is not a postal-address validator or a complete label layout. ## 8. Structure The base formatter has parameters `(prefix, name, uppercase)`. Binding positions one and three leaves `(name)`, which `for-each` calls for each supplied name. The formatter returns a text label. The optional pass-through stage uses `identity#1` for labels already prepared by an earlier stage. ## 9. Participants Customer attributes provide names. A configuration map supplies fixed argument values. The base formatter implements policy. The bound callback is reused by `for-each`. Identity supplies unchanged values in the alternative stage. ## 10. Collaborations Construct the bound callback outside the per-customer loop. Leave the varying name argument unbound, and check `function-arity` to make that contract explicit. If only the middle name argument is bound, the remaining callback parameters are `(prefix, uppercase)`, in that order. Bind every argument for a deferred call and invoke it with `()` to obtain the label. ## 11. Consequences Policy becomes explicit and reusable. Binding creates a callable, not its final result; invoking it performs formatting. Identity preserves values without normalization or validation. For node values it preserves the original node, and for maps/arrays it does not flatten their contents. No shipping action or file output occurs in these expressions. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One-based binding, residual argument order, all-bound and empty-map identity; Callable maps/arrays and bound-value conversion; String/nonpositive/out-of-arity key boundaries in the released profile. **Boundaries:** Current draft permits nonpositive integer keys and ignores them; the frozen positive-key refusal remains explicit. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new calls with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`; default XPath 3.1 rejects them. The placeholder and inline-identity comparisons use `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact report/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 fixtures. The source and customer inputs are complete, inline expressions. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Full synthetic dispatch input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 formatter](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/main.xpath): ```xpath let $names := parse-xml('')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.) let $format := function($prefix, $name, $uppercase) { concat($prefix, if ($uppercase) then upper-case(normalize-space($name)) else normalize-space($name)) } let $label := partial-apply($format, map {1: 'SHIP: ', 3: true()}) return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | ')) ``` Exact output: ```text arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 placeholder comparison](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $names := parse-xml('')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.) return let $format := function($prefix, $name, $uppercase) { concat($prefix, if ($uppercase) then upper-case(normalize-space($name)) else normalize-space($name)) } return let $label := $format('SHIP: ', ?, true()) return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | ')) ``` Exact output: ```text arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` ### Already formatted labels [Complete pass-through expression](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-labels.xpath): ```xpath let $labels := ('SHIP: ADA', 'SHIP: GRACE') return string-join(for-each($labels, identity#1), ' | ') ``` Exact output: ```text SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` The [3.1 identity callback comparison](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-baseline.xpath) uses `function($label) { $label }` and produces the identical output. ### Complete fixture inventory Each file supplies its complete input and exact report or error marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/main.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [baseline](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/baseline.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [preserve-case](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/preserve-case.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: Ada | SHIP: Grace` | | [empty-input](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/empty-input.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=` | | [all-bound](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/all-bound.xpath) | `arity=0; label=SHIP: ADA` | | [empty-bindings](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/empty-bindings.xpath) | `arity=3; label=SHIP: ADA` | | [remaining-order](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/remaining-order.xpath) | `arity=2; label=PICK: Ada` | | [ignored-high-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/ignored-high-key.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [bound-sequence](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/bound-sequence.xpath) | `FRAME+MOTOR` | | [callable-map](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/callable-map.xpath) | `ready` | | [callable-array](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/callable-array.xpath) | `express` | | [string-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/string-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [zero-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/zero-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [negative-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/negative-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [noncallable](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [bound-type-error](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/bound-type-error.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [identity-labels](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-labels.xpath) | `SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [identity-baseline](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-baseline.xpath) | `SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [identity-empty](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-empty.xpath) | `0` | | [identity-node](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-node.xpath) | `true` | | [identity-sequence](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-sequence.xpath) | `FRAME,MOTOR` | | [identity-container](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-container.xpath) | `true` | The case-preserving fixture binds `false()` and retains Ada/Grace capitalization. The empty dispatch fixture reports arity one and no labels. The all-bound fixture produces arity zero and one label when invoked. The remaining-order fixture binds Ada and calls the remaining `(prefix, uppercase)` parameters. The high-key fixture shows that position 99 is ignored. Sequence-valued bindings remain a single argument value, as the FRAME+MOTOR string-join example verifies. Identity cases cover empty, sequence, node and nested-container values. ## 14. Performance Bind configuration once and reuse the resulting function. Bosak captures bound argument values in a wrapper; this is not a memoization cache for formatter results. Label work still occurs on each invocation. Identity returns its supplied value unchanged. No benchmark or allocation-free pipeline claim follows from these examples. ## 15. Known Uses This batch-label workflow is a reproducible synthetic example. Existing evidence includes [`PartialApply_InlineFunctionBase`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_EmptyMap_ReturnsFunctionUnchanged`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_BindingAllArguments_YieldsZeroArityFunction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_KeysBeyondArity_AreIgnored`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_ArrayAsFunction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_BoundValueCoercion_FailsAtCallTimeWhenNoTypeMetadata`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_NonIntegerKey_RaisesXpty0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`Identity_ReturnsArgumentUnchanged`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exact `fn-identity` to GatedSets; no exact `fn-partial-apply` set is assigned. These 22 executable fixtures and named tests provide separate evidence. No gate membership changes are included. ## 16. Related Features [Higher-order selection](higher-order-selection.md) describes consumers of callbacks. [Product dependency closure](product-dependency-closure.md) applies a captured resolver callback to graph nodes. [Bounded retry state](bounded-retries.md) uses two-argument state callbacks. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks remaining names, separate from exhaustive signature coverage.

Full synthetic dispatch input:

```
