Consecutive partitioning

Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **Consecutive partitioning — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88) / [immutable revision `0a928bb8`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:partition](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-partition). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Split a dispatch queue into bounded batches while preserving arrival order. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 requires explicit recursion or stateful grouping logic to split at a boundary depending on the current partition. Grouping by route would merge nonadjacent orders, so it is not a semantics-preserving replacement for consecutive partitioning. partition returns a sequence of arrays. Its split callback receives the current nonempty partition sequence, next item and one-based input position. A true result starts the next partition before that item. Empty input returns no partitions; a singleton returns one array and the callback is not invoked for its first item. The worked chapter combines capacity and route-change boundaries. ## 5. Motivation Split a dispatch queue into bounded batches while preserving arrival order. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment This is consecutive splitting, not SQL GROUP BY and not a two-way accepted/rejected partition. Nonadjacent equal routes remain separate; filtering before splitting changes which boundaries are visible. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer opts into XPath40 and needs the exact validation or ordering contract described here. Keep the XPath 3.1 baseline when that opt-in is unavailable. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(partition(('NORTH','NORTH','NORTH','SOUTH','NORTH'), function($current,$next,$position) { count($current) ge 2 or $current[1] ne $next }) ! string-join(?*, ','), '|') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences partition returns a sequence of arrays. Its split callback receives the current nonempty partition sequence, next item and one-based input position. A true result starts the next partition before that item. Empty input returns no partitions; a singleton returns one array and the callback is not invoked for its first item. The worked chapter combines capacity and route-change boundaries. This is consecutive splitting, not SQL GROUP BY and not a two-way accepted/rejected partition. Nonadjacent equal routes remain separate; filtering before splitting changes which boundaries are visible. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Consecutive partition arrays preserve source order and nonadjacent groups; Split callback receives current partition, next item and original one-based position; Empty/singleton input avoids unnecessary predicate invocation. **Boundaries:** Not SQL grouping or a two-way filter; callback conversion beyond the tested signature remains a separate boundary. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [main.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/main.xpath): returns `NORTH,NORTH|NORTH|SOUTH|NORTH` at mode 40. [edge.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/edge.xpath): returns `0` at mode 40. [singleton.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/singleton.xpath): returns `1` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Duplicate checks and index selection may traverse the input; some/every may finish early. Partitioning creates arrays and retains input items. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `consecutive-partition-main`, `consecutive-partition-edge`, `consecutive-partition-singleton`. [`Partition_FixedSizeGroups`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Partition_SplitsOnValueChange`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Partition_EmptyInput_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) `fn-partition` is in GatedSets. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

functions/csv-parsing.md.text:
CSV parsing

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

## 1. Name and Classification **CSV parsing** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-123 CSV cluster; local FunctionLibrary CSV implementation. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:parse-csv](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-csv), [fn:csv-doc](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-csv-doc), [fn:csv-to-xml](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-csv-to-xml). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #104](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/104), [immutable mainline revision `e0024f5d`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/e0024f5d1d00c410e65ebf04f4caf89e770eb8ec) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use a dedicated CSV reader or an explicitly tested parser; tokenize is not a general CSV parser. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/csv-parsing/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/csv-parsing/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER,BLUE / 12` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A supplier exports product codes and quantities as quoted CSV cells. Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. **Options/defaults follow-up - 23 October 2026:** [Bounded review](../CSV-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [complete supplier import](../examples/csv-contracts/README.md) add99 catalog cases plus25 local-resource tests for published1.23.8. Omitted/empty options, headers, delimiters, ragged rows, validation and resource paths are covered. Non-positive selection conflicts with the current draft and frozen upstream test; unknown namespaced QName options also differ. These are explicit observations, not new support or full conformance. Historical adoption remains unassigned. ## 8. Structure ```xquery let $row := fn:parse-csv('"FILTER,BLUE",12')?rows[1] return $row?1 || ' / ' || $row?2 ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Absence versus empty/blank text and returned row/column records; Separator, quote, comment, trim, header and selection options; Local-resource base URI, encoding, errors and callback get bounds. **Boundaries:** Frozen positive selection/get indices differ from the current draft; unknown namespaced options remain unsupported; no remote-resource or schema-completeness claim. Follow-up groups: F03, F12. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. The baseline starts with a host-parsed array; it is not a replacement CSV parser. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/csv-parsing/main.xpath) yields `FILTER,BLUE / 12`. The [edge case](../examples/csv-parsing/edge.xpath) yields `FILTER,BLUE / 0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: input-size dependent. Parsing constructs row/cell values; the quantity cast and downstream business checks are separate costs. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses **Revision-specific index evidence:** [Audit](../CSV-INDEX-CONTRACT.md) reproduces124/0 frozen and117/7 current-upstream native cases. Upstream already changed selection and `get` expectations; adopting that contract is separate from this evidence-only audit. The original `observed-*` cases remain unchanged. Current applicable evidence: all `csv-contract-*` IDs in the [manifest](../examples/cases.json), the25 public API tests in [CsvResourceContractTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/CsvResourceContractTests.cs) (`LocalResource_UsesOptions`, `LocalResource_EncodingAndEmptyRows`, `LocalResource_PreservesErrors`, `MissingResource_RaisesFout1170`, `Keywords_ReadLocalResource`, `EmptySource_BypassesOptionInspection`) and existing [CsvTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/CsvTests.cs). All99 exact IDs are recorded in [the machine review](../CSV-CONTRACT-REVIEW.json). The existing `fn-parse-csv`, `fn-csv-to-xml`, `fn-csv-doc` gated sets apply within their frozen scope; `parse-csv-912` does not establish the opposite current-draft rule. No gate promotion or full current-draft certification follows. Executable example IDs: `csv-parsing-main`, `csv-parsing-edge`, `csv-parsing-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_CsvFunctions_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0017`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ParseCsv_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-csv-doc`, `fn-csv-to-xml`, `fn-parse-csv`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/customer-reference-matching.md.text:
Customer-reference Matching

21 October 2026

## 1. Name and Classification **Customer-reference equality and collation — existing 3.1 functions with reviewed 4.0 contracts.** Covers fn:distinct-values, fn:index-of, fn:deep-equal, fn:compare and fn:contains-token. Functions are not4.0-only names; this adds no name to the 117-name inventory. [REQ-126](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md) equality/collation documentation slice; [review and source pins](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), source base `5de2cfc5213529cdef419b9b7dec3cf9b6c03f7f`. Keyword syntax requires4.0. Unsupported draft forms are explicitly separated from supported calls. Documentation delivery: [Bosak PR #398](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/398). The review and verification receipts preserve source/specification pins, named cases, original findings and test hashes. ## 2. Intent Match synthetic customer references under an explicit business collation, retain every matching position, test whole tag tokens and verify report order. Start with the [complete customer example](../examples/equality-contracts/README.md). ## 3. Also Known As Equivalence classes, positional lookup, structural equality, three-way comparison and token membership are different operations, not interchangeable function aliases. The current compare parameter-name drift is not an accepted rename of the specification. ## 4. History / Supersedes All five names exist in 3.1. The [positional3.1 report](../examples/equality-contracts/report-normal-31.xpath) and [keyword4.0 report](../examples/equality-contracts/report-normal-40.xpath) give the same stated output.4.0 expands compare to atomic operands and deep-equal to optional options; this review does not claim full implementation of those declarations. Current pins do not reconstruct historical adoption. ## 5. Motivation Case-insensitive matching does not imply accent folding, Unicode normalization, substring matching, unordered sequence equality or case-insensitive map keys. Make each import policy observable instead of conflating those decisions. ## 6. Language Alignment JavaScript Set and .NET Distinct are only rough analogies. XPath distinct-value representative/order rules are not a promise of insertion order; index-of returns all one-based positions; deep-equal is sequence/order-sensitive and does not mean reference identity. NaN behavior differs between value equality and deep equality. Culture/default comparer behavior from host languages must not silently select a business collation. ## 7. Applicability Use supported explicit string collations for a declared reference/tag contract. Use codepoint comparison for identifiers whose spelling must remain exact. Do not use this miniature report as identity verification, a production schema, or fuzzy customer matching. Validate required/unique IDs separately. ## 8. Structure ```xquery distinct-values($references, $collation) index-of($references, $target, $collation) compare($reference, $target, $collation) eq 0 contains-token($tags, $token, $collation) deep-equal($actualIds, $expectedIds) ``` Full argument types/defaults and options differences are in the [signature audit](../audit-equality-collation-contracts.json). Collaborations parse-xml supplies controlled input; simple mapping projects strings without imposing path-node order; explicit NFC normalization is optional policy, not collation preprocessing. The report combines all five operations while keeping membership, positions, identity and order separate. ## 11. Consequences Explicit policy makes reports reproducible for the supplied supported collations. Case folding can collapse distinct business identifiers if chosen incorrectly. ASCII collation does not fold Ä/ä or normalize combining marks. A distinct count is deliberately used without relying on which duplicate spelling or order is returned. ## 12. NaN behavior differs between value equality and deep equality. Culture/default comparer behavior from host languages must not silently select a business collation.
